Sports.title: Warrington and Leeds win as Super League play-offs approach
Sports.content:
Warrington claimed their fifth consecutive Betfred Super League win with a 34-24 victory over Huddersfield Giants at Halliwell Jones Stadium.

Huddersfield took the lead when Sam Halsall scooped up the ball and went over, but George Flanagan was unable to convert.

Danny Walker replied for the Wire, with Leon Hayes adding the extras to send them in front, and the hosts soon took charge.

Image: Matty Ashton scores for Warrington

In the 28th minute, James Bentley latched onto a quick offload from James Harrison to cross and Sam Powell grounded just two minutes later, with Hayes converting both tries.

Warrington continued to pile on the pressure when George Williams finished off a move down the left flank as they sailed to a 22-4 lead at the break.

After the restart, Halsall scored his second try of the match after holding Adam Clune's kick to cross, with Flanagan converting, but Arron Lindop replied for Warrington and Hayes scored a penalty to extend their advantage further.

Image: Warrington have confirmed a playoff place

Huddersfield continued to apply pressure as Sam Hewitt's try was converted and Connor Wrench then struck after touching down in the corner to close the gap.

Warrington were able to wrap up victory in the last 10 minutes when Matty Ashton grounded and Hayes converted, but the Giants continued to battle until the end when when Jacob Gagai crossed for their fifth try of the afternoon in the final minutes.

Leeds cruise to comprehensive win over York

Image: Harry Newman thanks the Leeds fans and supporters after the victory at York

Leeds returned to the top of Super League after cruising to a comprehensive 66-16 victory over York Knights at the LNER Community Stadium.

Riley Lumb scored three tries and Chris Hankinson added two of his own as well as four conversions as the Rhinos responded instantly to Wigan moving above them on Friday night.

Kallum Watkins, Mikolaj Oledzki, Lachie Miller, Matt Lodge, Ryan Hall, Brodie Croft and Ash Handley were Leeds' other try-scorers, while Jake Connor added another quartet of conversions and Miller one.

Image: Riley Lumb celebrates after scoring his hat-trick try against York

Sam Wood, Jon Bennison - who also converted two tries - and David Nofoaluma ensured York would not be shut out.

Lumb had to wait for a review after dotting down in the corner, but his seventh-minute opening try was ultimately confirmed before he acrobatically added his second five minutes later.

Rhinos had taken a 36-0 lead by half-time thanks to Hankinson's first - teed up by Lumb - three minutes later, before Watkins got in on the action, Oledzki added a close-range try and Miller got on the end of Cameron Smith's excellent pass.

Image: Ash Handley scores his try for Leeds

Lodge scored his debut try two minutes after the break before Wood finally put points on the board for York. However, Rhinos quickly hit back through Hall ahead of Lumb completing his hat-trick.

Lumb touched down for a fourth time four minutes after the hour as Rhinos kept piling on the points, ensuring two more York tries through Bennison and Nofoaluma counted for little.

Sports.title: 'This is harsh times' - Wolff defends ordering Russell to let Antonelli past
Sports.content:
Mercedes chief Toto Wolff insists it was "not a difficult decision" to order George Russell to allow team-mate Kimi Antonelli past him during the Dutch Grand Prix.

Championship leader Antonelli was running second to Lando Norris with 16 laps to go when Mercedes decided to pit the Italian for fresh tyres under a virtual safety car, bringing him out in third behind Russell.

It quickly became apparent that Antonelli didn't have the pace to challenge Norris for victory, but while he soon closed up on Russell, the difficulty of overtaking at Zandvoort meant there was no guarantee the Italian would be able to cruise past his team-mate.

However, Russell was told over the radio to allow Antonelli through into second, which would leave the Brit vulnerable to losing his place on the podium to Lewis Hamilton, on fresh tyres behind him with his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc in tow.

With the help of another VSC interruption, Russell did brilliantly to hold off Hamilton, but finishing behind Antonelli meant the gap between them at the top of the championship increased to 59 points.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes team-mates Kimi Antonelli and George Russell reflect on their Dutch Grand Prix race.

Wolff told Sky Sports F1: "We had a free stop with Kimi - a team internal free stop - and George was incredibly at the end fighting and also fending off the Ferraris, who were on a much quicker car. Was really, really exceptional.

"That (the decision) looks difficult on the outside but not on the inside. It's a situation we discussed very often, also today in the morning 'we're not going to lose time fighting with each other and have two Ferraris breathing down our neck'.

"So, it would have been the other way around exactly the same. It plays no role who is ahead in the championship or not, it's just about protecting the best possible positions."

Wolff insisted that his focus has to be on the best result for the team, rather than worrying about the feelings of his drivers.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris hunted down Kimi Antonelli and Lewis Hamilton to take the race lead at the Dutch Grand Prix.

"I don't think Antonelli was anywhere near catching Norris," Wolff added.

"It was just the safest way in terms of scoring points. You could have played maybe leaving him in the Overtake Mode and then again, you are risking too much, you have two Ferraris all over you.

"So, it was some tough calls, but they need to be done when you want to fight for the constructors' and drivers' championship.

"This is how we are operating. Both drivers know that. We avoid situations like some other teams where it's not clearly talked like this.

"This is harsh times, there's 2,500 people who work for championships, and it's not one man's game. That's how we operate it the last 15 years."

Russell: Antonelli deserved second

Russell initially appeared to question the order over the radio as he asked whether Antonelli had a chance of catching Norris, but ultimately quickly followed the instruction.

Asked about his thought process at the time, Russell said: "We've always said as a team, when we're on different strategies, we're never going to fight and we're always going to invert, and that's always just been our sort of rules.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen loses control of his car at the beginning of the race and hits into the wall at the Dutch Grand Prix.

"And the fact is Kimi was ahead of me before the VSC and he tried something different to protect us as a team. He kind of copy-pasted what the Ferraris did.

"Could I have kept him behind? Maybe. But equally, it could have been a P5 as well.

"So, in the end, he deserved to be P2. I think P3 was a fair result for me."

Antonelli: George made my life a lot easier

Antonelli thanked Russell for obeying the team order but admitted he felt as though his strategy had put his team-mate at greater risk of losing a podium.

The 19-year-old took the lead by passing Norris at an early restart but was unable to match the McLaren driver's impressive pace once they switched to the hard tyre compound at the first round of pit stops.

Antonelli said: "It was a difficult second half (of the race) for me, especially in the last stint on the hards, just really struggling. Had little confidence in the car and, yeah, it was not easy.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Ferrari team-mates nearly came together in the final stages of the race as Lando Norris took the Dutch GP victory.

"And then obviously we pitted, and also that was a bit tricky. But then also George, I have to thank him because he made my life a lot easier.

"But I still think probably could have stayed out and gone until the end with the same set because it put us a little bit at risk. Also, I feel we put George at risk with having to let me by and everything.

"But I still think, at the end of the day, it was a great team execution with how things were, and I think today P2 was the maximum we could have done because the pace of the McLarens, especially in the second half, was just too strong."

Sports.title: 'Could have been a lot worse' - Verstappen relieved after huge crash
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen admitted his huge crash at the Dutch Grand Prix "could have been a lot worse" after he lost control of his Red Bull on the opening lap of his final home event.

Verstappen caught too much of the damp kerb through the normally flat-out banked corner and hit the outside barriers hard before coming to a halt in front of a packed Zandvoort crowd.

The severity of the incident caused a red flag but Verstappen walked away unharmed from what is likely to be the last Dutch Grand Prix of his career - as the event does not have a contract beyond this year.

"It was of course still quite wet in that corner. As soon as I was going through the corner, I could see a little bit of a dry line coming, and I thought from that point on I could accelerate again, but it suddenly then accelerated a lot," Verstappen explained to Sky Sports F1.

"It caught me out, simple as that. I tried to correct it but couldn't. And then you hit the wall, but it could have been a lot worse because there were a lot of cars behind me as well, but luckily that all went well."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Verstappen analyses his crash which took him out of the Dutch Grand Prix early on

Rosberg on Verstappen's crash Sky Sports F1's Nico Rosberg



"It's wet, dry, it's a mix of everything. It's incredibly difficult on slick tyres to drive through this high-speed, fast corner. It's the hardest thing in the world.



"Max is clearly tighter than everybody else and when you look more closely it looks like the dry patch is offset about 50 centimetres from the inside.



"I think he just put a bit too much throttle down and you're gone. He's the greatest driver out there, one of the greatest of all time, that just goes to show how difficult it is in these conditions.



"Probably that was Max's mistake."

Verstappen: Zandvoort highlighted Red Bull are fourth fastest

It was a dramatic end to a disappointing first race after the summer break for Red Bull, just days after Verstappen signed a new contract to stay with the team until at least the end of 2030.

Verstappen started and finish Saturday's Sprint in sixth and was half a second behind pace-setters Mercedes and McLaren in both qualifying sessions.

Having been able to compete at the front in the four races before the summer break, with three podiums in July, it was a surprise to see Red Bull take a step back.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nico Rosberg discusses Verstappen's contract extension with Red Bull, saying it's a 'super important message' for the team

"If you look on average the whole season we have been fourth fastest, I think this weekend really highlighted that," said Verstappen.

"We're a little bit behind, we want to be closer. Maybe [at the next race] in Monza we are, but I don't know.

"We're getting towards the end of the season, you also have to look at next year. I think there are a few things on the car we are looking at that can only be changed next year, to really find a lot more performance."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Sky Sports F1 team discuss why Verstappen has stayed at Red Bull

Red Bull did not bring a major upgrade to Zandvoort, only a new front corner, so team boss Laurent Mekies says they need to understand if their lack of performance was circuit specific, or to do with previous upgrades.

"Performance-wise I think there is nowhere to hide. It was a very difficult weekend. It seems we have made a bit of a step back compared to where we were before the summer break," he said.

"Of course we will never know what the real pace of the car would have been with Max. It's fair to say session after session it looked more difficult than it was in Budapest or Spa or Austria."

Sports.title: Liverpool’s Szoboszlai spot on with late, late leveller to salvage point at Newcastle
Sports.content:
Before kick-off a banner was raised in the Gallowgate End inscribed with a quotation from the late Kevin Keegan. “I want people to dream about their football,” it read. “We should all be dreamers at heart.”

Out on the pitch it swiftly became apparent that both Matthias Jaissle, Keegan’s latest successor in the Newcastle dugout, and Liverpool’s new manager Andoni Iraola are on individual missions to create forms of organised chaos capable of subjecting the best opponents to torrid nightmares.

Despite a few, ultimately forlorn, attempts to introduce semblances of control on the parts of the visiting playmaker Florian Wirtz and Newcastle’s elegant central midfielder Lewis Miley, this was sheer, unadulterated, mutual mayhem of the sort to make Iraola’s more purist Anfield predecessor Arne Slot wince.

Along the way to a draw secured, perhaps slightly fortuitously, by Dominik Szoboszlai’s 99th-minute penalty for Liverpool, the returning former Newcastle striker Alexander Isak left minimal imprint on a match that had been supposed to be all about him. Instead Isak was upstaged by Jaissle’s forward William Osula.

No sooner had the heartfelt tributes to Keegan, a player and manager adored by both clubs, been completed it very quickly became apparent that Jérémy Jacquet and Virgil van Dijk had no answers to Osula as the young Dane turned and accelerated towards goal following Ryan Gravenberch’s inexplicable surrender of possession.

The stage was set for this most unpredictable of strikers to spot Anthony Elanga, then in the process of leaving Milos Kerkez for dust down the right, slide a pass in the winger’s direction and watch as, a steadying touch later, Elanga’s shot flashed beyond Alisson’s reach.

Only five minutes had passed, Jaissle’s tenure as Newcastle’s manager was off to perfect start and already Iraola looked distinctly stressed.

His defence did not convince, with Kerkez finding few answers to Elanga. Like Jaissle, Iraola is a high priest of pressing but Liverpool’s best hope here seemed to be to retain possession, impose their technical superiority and out-pass Newcastle.

Significantly their best moments coincided largely with those albeit sporadic occasions when Wirtz –who would be withdrawn midway through the second half – managed to get on the ball and began unnerving a Newcastle side supposedly in the throes of a dramatic transition.

It is only three weeks since Jaissle succeeded Eddie Howe but the former Al-Ahli manager has certainly succeeded in not merely re-energising a mentally jaded team but sharpening a swarm pressing game that had become more than a little half hearted and untidy. “The manager is top,” said Elanga. “Playing for him is fun.”

Given that Jaissle has inherited a team shorn of last season’s luminaries – Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães – this achievement was all the more impressive. The 38-year-old German trusted 18-year-old Sean Steur, recently arrived from Ajax, alongside Miley in the key holding roles in his 4-2-3-1 system and for long periods they held their own.

View image in fullscreen Newcastle and Liverpool fans pay tribute to Kevin Keegan, who died last month. Keegan played for both clubs and managed Newcastle. Photograph: Newcastle United/Getty Images

Behind them, Malick Thiaw and Sven Botman excelled in central defence while Amar Dedic shone at right-back following his £30m move from Benfica.

There are ways to leave a football club but the route Isak chose – mounting a one-man strike before forcing a record £125m move to Liverpool last summer – ensured he was greeted by chants of “rat, rat, rat,” as he alighted from the visiting team bus.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

If Isak seemed quite unconcerned – he grinned broadly in the face of some further sustained hostility before kick-off – the Sweden striker added to Iraola’s problems by miscuing his sole chance of an alarmingly anonymous afternoon. Instead it was a forward facing an uncertain future at Anfield who kept Liverpool in it. When Jaissle’s midfield inexplicably stood off him Cody Gakpo’s first time shot from outside the area defied Lukas Hornicek.

View image in fullscreen Joe Willock’s superb finish, found despite the attentions of several Liverpool players, had looked like being the winning goal. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

With Osula now limping, on came Joe Willock for Newcastle leaving the impressive Yoane Wissa – arguably man of the match – to shift from the No 10 to No 9 role. Willock is reportedly close to joining Besiktas but delighted in immediately offering a reminder of his enduring worth on Tyneside.

When Wissa, rather wonderfully, dodged three supposed markers his ensuing pass to Willock was superbly calibrated and the latter returned the compliment by curling a shot past Alisson and in off a post. Tellingly, Willock was mobbed by every outfield teammate with Nick Woltemade and his fellow home substitutes racing the length of the pitch to congratulate him.

Quick Guide How do I 

Low on creativity, Liverpool seemed beaten until deep in injury time the substitute Victor Muñoz was felled when the otherwise convincing Newcastle left-back Lewis Hall rather unluckily caught his knee in the penalty area.

All that remained was for Szoboszlai to lash his ensuing penalty high into the roof of the net and level a game as swashbuckling as anything even Keegan might have conjured.

Sports.title: ‘Call his agent’: Emery feels Watkins should explain absence from Villa’s rout by Brighton
Sports.content:
Unai Emery did nothing to deny that Ollie Watkins had refused to play for Aston Villa in their sobering 4-0 defeat by Brighton at the Amex on Sunday. The head coach had a selection crisis up front with Brian Madjo and Tammy Abraham injured. However, he did not include Watkins in the matchday squad as the England striker considers a move to Al-Hilal in Saudi Arabia.

Emery was forced to rely on the attacking midfielder Emiliano Buendía as an emergency striker and his team disappeared without trace on the south coast. They were 4-0 down after 31 minutes and had their new signing João Gomes sent off on his debut in the 40th minute. Gomes kicked up and out at the Brighton striker Georginio Rutter after being dispossessed by him.

Al-Hilal have made a number of bids for Watkins, all of which have been rejected. It is understood the 30-year-old is open to the move and Emery talked on Friday like a manager who was realistic about the sale happening. Villa would plainly like to replace Watkins should he depart as they approach the end of another difficult summer window. They have already sold Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne and Youri Tielemans, while they are expected to move on Emiliano Martínez.

Emery was asked why he had not picked Watkins against Brighton. “This question is for him,” he said. “I can answer only with my silence.” Emery was then asked if Watkins had refused to play, to which he said: “I think you can call him and you can call his agent and he can respond.”

The Guardian have contacted Watkins’s agent for comment.

“He [Watkins] can only explain his answer, I can’t,” Emery added, after being asked if he felt let down by Watkins.

Emery reported that Madjo would be out for “two weeks more … more or less” while attacking midfielder Johan Manzambi – who has been the club’s marquee summer signing – would “need maybe some days more [than that]”. He was unclear about a timeframe for Abraham’s return.

Quick Guide How do I 

Emery talked up the resistance of his players in the second half against Brighton and said he was optimistic about finding solutions for the season ahead. But he returned to the difficult preparations for the opening fixture, noting that: “Two strikers are injured and another striker gives his answer.”

The head coach added: “This problem [with the transfer market] … we had every season and every season we overcame it. It’s something we have to accept and always we reacted, especially the players. This is something hard for us every year but we are calm. With this result, it’s more difficult to explain but calm, work, be positive and find solutions for the next week and after the transfer window.”

Sports.title: Maresca concedes Manchester City ‘a work in progress’ after hair-raising escape
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca said Manchester City remain a “work in progress” after Sunday’s last-gasp win over Bournemouth at the Etihad Stadium.

Marc Guéhi’s 85th-minute equaliser and Josko Gvardiol’s 91st-minute winner gave City’s new manager victory in his first game, after Marcus Tavernier’s first-half strike for the visitors.

Maresca thought his side performed similarly to last Sunday’s 3-0 Community Shield loss to Arsenal. “I feel in the same position as after Arsenal,” the Italian said. “It’s normal you judge after results but I don’t see big changes. Unfortunately, this is a work in progress and I’m looking for solutions. For sure when you win games it helps.

“If you think of the Premier League – it won’t happen that you will concede nothing. The goal we conceded was their first shot. They had two or three dangerous moments but it’s how you react. We’ve still got [Erling] Haaland, Elliot [Anderson], Marc [Guéhi], Nico O’Reilly [who all started], who are in pre-season still. It’s a huge difference in terms of physicality and we are going to get better and better.”

Before the game City unfurled a huge tifo bearing his image that said: “Welcome back Enzo.” He said: “It is the perfect day. I was very pleased to see the banner when the game started. We gave them [fans] the joy at the end. It was quite emotional. The spirit was fantastic. It’s a game we deserved to win [but] you don’t need to wait for the last five minutes. We missed chances, then they scored and it became more complicated.”

Maresca fielded Guéhi in an unfamiliar midfield role. “I know Marc from [ Crystal] Palace and I always thought he could play as a midfielder because he is very good,” the manager said. “So we tried it for a few days and I think he was quite good. He gives us a solution for the future,.”

In his first game managing Bournemouth, Marco Rose came close to leading them to a first away win against City. “We’re competitors, we came here to win for the first time,” said the German. “We were in a good way to do so. But we did many good things. We have a lot of things to improve. At the end, how the game went was quite unlucky to lose that way. We had two situations – one corner kick and one attacking [move] – when we defended too passively.

“We need to defend the corner better and the second goal was just too passive. We always try to push up – we want to defend higher. Here you need to find the right triggers and it’s hard to press. We did it really well until the end.”

Sports.title: Manchester City agree deal worth up to €100m for Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi
Sports.content:
Manchester City have agreed a deal with Lille worth €95m (£81.4m) plus €5m in potential add-ons for Ayyoub Bouaddi, with the Morocco midfielder’s arrival to take the club’s summer spend to nearly £200m after Elliot Anderson’s £116m signing earlier in the window.

The 18-year-old was stood down from Lille’s Ligue 1 match against Angers on Sunday before a medical with City and his transfer becoming official in the next few days.

Bouaddi, who operates mainly as a No 6, started five of Morocco’s six games at the World Cup tournament this summer, including the 2-0 quarter-final defeat by France. That was only his eighth international appearance. His Lille debut came in an October 2023 Conference League group game– at 16 years and three days, it made him the youngest footballer to play in the competition.

The majority of the fee for Bouaddi will come from the £65m sale of Rodri to Barcelona, which was sealed last week.

Anderson, who is making his debut in City’s Premier League opener against Bournemouth on Sunday, can play as No 6 or No 8, so Bouaddi may not go directly into Enzo Maresca’s starting XI.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

City remain interested in Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández, also a midfielder. The west London club want £120m for the Argentinian but City are thought to value him at a lower figure.

Sports.title: European football: Mohamed Salah scores first goals in Trabzonspor victory
Sports.content:
Mohamed Salah scored his first goals for Trabzonspor with a brace in their 2-1 win over Istanbul Basaksehir.

The former Liverpool forward joined the Super Lig side on a two-year deal at the start of August and made his debut for the club from the bench in their 1-1 draw at Kasimpasa last week.

Salah was named in the starting lineup for Sunday’s clash with Basaksehir and made an instant impact, opening the scoring in the eighth minute.

Basaksehir levelled in the 19th minute when Eldor Shomurodov slotted home from the penalty spot, but Salah restored his side’s lead just three minutes into the second half. His brace was enough to clinch victory for Trabzonspor, who return to Super Lig action on 31 August against Amed SK.

Atlético Madrid salvaged a 2-2 draw against Villarreal in La Liga despite having defender Robin Le Normand sent off. Giuliano Simeone grabbed his team a draw after penalties from Gerard Moreno and Georges Mikautadze put Villarreal in front following Marc Pubill’s 59th-minute opener for the hosts.

The Atlético head coach, Diego Simeone, brought Julián Alvarez on as a second-half substitute to a chorus of boos from home supporters. The forward walked down the tunnel alone at the end, while his teammates were thanking the Atlético supporters.

View image in fullscreen Julián Alvarez leaves the pitch at the end of the game after Atlético Madrid fans booed him during the 2-2 draw with Villarreal. Photograph: Europa Press Sports/Europa Press/Getty Images

“We all have to be united, Julián is with us in the team, while he’s here we will support him,” said the Atlético goalkeeper, Jan Oblak. “It’s not a comfortable situation for anyone, I hope it’s resolved and we’re all happy at the end of the season.”

Juventus secured a 1-0 away win against newly promoted Frosinone, but failed to impress in their opening match of the Serie A season.

Juve, who finished sixth last season, secured all three points thanks to Gleison Bremer’s 22nd-minute header. Luciano Spalletti’s side went on to dominate but failed to put the game beyond doubt.

The goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario, on loan from Tottenham, picked up a leg injury and had to be substituted late on, which nearly cost Juve as Frosinone pressed hard in stoppage time, hitting the crossbar.

View image in fullscreen Juventus centre-back Gleison Bremer heads home the only goal of the game against Frosinone. Photograph: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images

Another of the newly promoted teams, Monza, were thrashed 4-1 by champions Inter on Saturday in the season opener.

Lecce made a strong start to the season against the third promoted side, Venezia, on Sunday as they defeated their hosts 2-0 courtesy of second-half goals from Olaf Gorter and Tiago Gabriel.

The Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane was voted the 2026 player of the year in Germany by an association of sports journalists on Sunday, finishing ahead of teammate Michael Olise. Kicker magazine revealed the results of its yearly polls of members of the Association of German Sports Journalists. Kane, the England captain, won the award after a stellar season in which he won the Bundesliga and German Cup while Bayern also reached the Champions League semi-finals. Bayern’s Vincent Kompany was named coach of the year, while their women’s captain, Giulia Gwinn, won the award for best female player.

Sports.title: West Brom surge back to floor Flemming-less Burnley amid transfer speculation
Sports.content:
West Brom’s head coach, James Morrison, insisted his side must “stay humble” after Isaac Price inspired them to a 3-1 comeback win against promotion favourites Burnley in the Championship at the Hawthorns. The Northern Ireland international scored twice in the second half after setting up Harry Whitwell’s equaliser to cancel out Callum Styles’s early own goal.

“I felt it was a top performance. I enjoyed it at times for the intensity with the lads willing to run for each other,” Morrison said. “We did the basics really well – we won tackles, and when we lost the ball, we ran back and when the opportunities were given to us, we took advantage.

“I felt like Burnley couldn’t handle our intensity, and I could smell that at half-time, so the message was to up the intensity.”

Burnley, without injured star striker Zian Flemming amid intense speculation of a move, failed to match their lofty billing in a disappointing second-half display. Albion continued their 100% start to the season, gaining their third straight win in all competitions and second in the league to lie second in the early table, behind Millwall on goal difference.

In a fast and furious start, there were two goals in the first 18 minutes. Styles put into his own net in the eighth minute from Jacob Bruun Larsen’s cross. Albion complained that Hannibal Mejbri fouled Felix Horn Myhre in the buildup 70 yards away, with several passages of play unfolding before the goal. Styles had to make contact to prevent Oliver Sonne getting the chance but the ball hit his left heel and it flew into the net.

Whitwell equalised on 18 minutes when he slotted home low to Max Weiss’s left from 12 yards for the 20-year-old’s first league goal for Albion. Burnley appeared wrongfooted by Jimmy-Jay Morgan’s flick-on from Price’s cross, before Bashir Humphreys failed to clear. But it was Burnley who went closest to scoring again when Bruun Larsen sidefooted against the foot of the post from Marcus Edwards’s searching cross.

View image in fullscreen Harry Whitwell’s strike pulls the Baggies level. Photograph: Ryan Browne/Shutterstock

It was a different story after the break. Inspired by Price, Albion produced a dominant second-half performance, with the perfect start. Price put them ahead for the first time, in the 46th minute, curling the ball beyond Weiss, who had strayed five yards off his line, into the far corner. The goal came from a loose ball when Morgan tried to help back Styles’s cross and Hannibal challenged.

Burnley made a triple change in the 57th minute with the arrival of Ugo Raghouber, Zeki Amdouni, and Dastan Satpayev. Amdouni tried to test Max O’Leary with a rising, curling effort from 20 yards but it flew straight at the Albion keeper.

Instead it was Albion who struck next to effectively seal it, after Humphreys upended Whitwell for a clear penalty. Price made no mistake from the spot, firing low to Weiss’s right with the keeper going the wrong way.

Afterwards, Morrison said: “We enjoy competing against the so-called bigger teams and we competed really well today. We don’t want to get carried away. We have to keep our feet on the ground, keep working hard and stay humble.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Burnley head coach, Nicky Hayen, said: “I think we didn’t have the energy, desire and hunger of the home team. You also have to give credit to West Brom. You can always say we played a bad game but they had the structure, a lot of good energy, hunger and desire.

“We had problems and no solutions. I didn’t expect this – it was an eye-opener for everyone, myself included.

Morrison went on to defend Aune Heggebø, as the Norway striker missed Sunday’s game following his retrospective Football Association two-match ban for “deception of a match official”. The sanction came after the incident against Norwich when his goal went in off his hand. Albion have appealed against the ban.

“We were really frustrated and shocked. Bo was disappointed so we had to back him and we wanted to appeal,” said Morrison. “He was deemed to have cheated the referee which he didn’t. Yes the ball hit his hand but with the pace of the cross and the keeper touching it, it’s very hard to get out of the way.”

Sports.title: Hull punished United defence in victory but Carrick’s attack is bigger area of concern | Andrew Beasley
Sports.content:
Hull scored nine league goals from set plays last season, the joint-fewest in the Championship. Yet two in 21 minutes earned them a victory over Manchester United on Saturday.

It was a disastrous start to the campaign for the visitors. While Michael Carrick said before the game it would not be easy, he would not have expected victory being so straightforward for Hull. It was a match United simply had to win given the gulf in resources and expectation. Opta rated their chance of victory at 68.9% before kick-off.

United’s inability to deal with Oli McBurnie as the target man was painful to watch. Their slack defending on the set pieces from which Hull scored will also draw focus. Their attacking should be the greatest concern, though.

A glance at expected goal numbers can paint a false impression. Hull generated 1.01 expected goals to United’s 1.83, so did the visitors deserve to win? The issue is the breakdown of chances that contributed to the total. United had 21 shots, 16 of which were worth less than 0.1 expected goals.

This was a theme last season, albeit less obvious when they performed well under Carrick. United’s open-play shots were worth an average of 0.104 expected goals in 2025-26, the third worst rate among teams that finished in the top half of the Premier League. Against Hull, this figure was just 0.087.

Not until the 78th minute did a notable opportunity fall to a player they would hope to have one, as Bryan Mbeumo received a through ball from Matheus Cunha. Before that, their highest-value chances fell to Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui. The former has experience as a winger, and started in the attacking midfield trio in United’s 4-2-3-1 formation, but the duo have just 16 top-flight goals between them. They are not reliable chance converters.

Marcus Rashford is far stronger. He should take Dorgu’s berth in the long term, assuming he remains with the club. His natural attacking instincts may have aided in the creation of better chances in the first half. Regardless, it was alarming how hard United found it to fashion valuable opportunities against a club that conceded the second-most expected goals in the 2025-26 Championship.

Hull’s manager, Sergej Jakirovic, used a back five. He deployed three centre-backs on 10 occasions last season, notably in victories in the playoff semi-final second leg against Millwall and the final against Middlesbrough.

It worked against United, with the extra bodies at the back able to crowd out attackers. Opta’s shot map showed Hull conceded eight efforts in the “danger zone” – the centre of the penalty area that covers the width of the six-yard box out to the 18-yard line. Five of the eight were headers, which are harder to convert, leaving little else of note. Space in the most valuable real estate came at a premium at the MKM Stadium and United were unable to penetrate it.

This structure has caused United problems before. They have now won only one of their last six league matches against teams that started with a back three or five. Leeds won 2-1 at Old Trafford in April with a 3-4-3 formation and used the same system to draw 1-1 two weeks ago in a pre-season friendly. Milan employed the same framework when beating United 4-2 in their final warm-up game.

“We got beat, we’re hurt and it’s not a nice feeling. It doesn’t mean it’s going to change the whole direction of how we’re going as a team or as a football club,” Carrick said. As sensible a long-term approach as that may be, United’s attack needs work.

Sports.title: Mateta’s Palace dispute deepens after losing appeals to end contract early
Sports.content:
Jean-Philippe Mateta is in dispute with Crystal Palace over the final year of his contract but failed in an attempt to have it ruled invalid by an independent Premier League tribunal and Fifa. The France striker signed a four-and-a-half-year contract when he joined permanently from Mainz in January 2022 after an initial loan, in a deal that also included the option of a 12-month extension. That was activated by Palace in 2024, with Mateta’s contract now due to expire at the end of this season.

But it is understood the 29-year-old and his representatives have disputed whether that extension was valid and took the case to an independent tribunal under Premier League regulations last season. Official confirmation of the outcome has not been disclosed, although Palace insist Mateta’s contract remains binding and he played in their defeat at Everton on Saturday. Fifa also rejected his claim after ruling it did not have jurisdiction over the dispute. Mateta’s representative has been approached for comment.

Quick Guide How do I 

Mateta has been trying to force through a move from Selhurst Park for some time and it is understood he has interest from Aston Villa, who are considering whether to sell Ollie Watkins to the Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal. Mateta failed a medical with Milan in January because of a knee problem after the Italian side had agreed a fee of around £30m and spent two months on the sidelines before returning to help Palace win the Conference League. Mateta was booed by some sections of supporters at first and is likely to get another frosty reception when Manchester City visit south London on Friday night in their first home match of the new campaign.

View image in fullscreen Jean-Philippe Mateta had a shot hit a post during Crystal Palace’s defeat at Everton. Photograph: Paul Currie/Shutterstock

Meanwhile, Pierre Sage has insisted that Ismaïla Sarr will remain at the club despite strong interest from Galatasaray. The Senegal forward missed the 2-0 defeat at Everton due to what Sage described as a “pain in his groin” and Palace’s new manager dismissed reports that the 28-year-old had refused to travel to Merseyside because he wants to leave.

“We took the decision before the session with the doctor, the player, and me, to let him get treatment and do an individual session, and he will be back on Monday with us,” he said. “For the moment, we don’t want him to leave. He is under contract with us with three years to go and he will be with us on Monday.”

Palace are also braced for more interest this week in Adam Wharton and Daniel Muñoz, who has entered the final two years of his contract and has been linked with Everton, Nottingham Forest and Tottenham. They have already agreed a loan move for Chelsea’s Axel Disasi but may be forced into signing another centre back before the deadline if fears over Chadi Riad’s knee injury are proved correct.

The Moroccan, who was out for more than a year after suffering an anterior cruciate ligament injury on his second appearance for the club after joining in 2024, was carried off on a stretcher after attempting to block a cross in the second half against Everton. “I hope it will be better than we think,” said Sage. “We await the medical tests.”

Sports.title: New claims emerge from the women involved in the Sydney Swans hotel saga
Sports.content:
New claims emerge from the women involved in the Sydney Swans hotel saga

One of the three women at the centre of the Sydney Swans hotel saga has reportedly made a second sexual assault allegation.

Sex Crimes Squad detectives have been investigating 'a report of a sexual assault' at the Pullman East Melbourne hotel last Monday, according to Victoria Police.

However, one women represented by law firm Slater & Gordon has now alleged she was the victim of 'multiple sexual assaults' while in the hotel, The Age reports.

The fresh allegation follows two other women, represented by Carbone Lawyers, claiming they were subjected to sexual conduct in excess of what was agreed to when they were booked as topless waitresses.

Slater & Gordon lawyer Jackson Pannam said on Saturday that the firm had been asked by his client to determine if there was any basis for a civil claim.

'Everyone deserves to be safe going about their life, at home, at work and in public spaces without risk of being assaulted or harmed,' he said in a statement.

It's understood Slater & Gordon lawyer said the new allegation has been reported to police. When asked specifically if the investigation had been broadened, a Victoria Police spokesperson told The Age: 'We have nothing further to add.'

The Sydney Swans have stood down players Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, Riley Bice and James Jordon for the remainder of the AFL season.

Sydney Swans players who were not involved in the hotel incident took to the field on Sunday night for a much-needed win against North Melbourne to boost morale

Diehard Swans fans showed their support for the team during the clash

Some players broke into tears as the siren sounded on the fourth quarter on Sunday after an incredibly tough week for the team

However the club says that sanction was for breaching team standards by staying out late, drinking and calling the women to the hotel, and makes no judgement on the sexual assault allegations, saying that is for police to determine.

Daily Mail does not suggest any of the named Swans players are under police investigation or involved in any wrongdoing alleged by the women.

There have been reports that up to nine people were in the hotel room.

The Swans have maintained no more than five of its players or staff were there.

No charges have been laid and the investigation 'remains active and ongoing'.

According to Mr Pannam, the woman, who contacted police immediately after the alleged assault, has had her world turned upside down and is navigating an 'incredibly traumatic experience'.

'We will be putting all of the relevant parties on notice in due course,' he earlier told reporters.

'We're standing with our client to give her support at this difficult time and to help her get the justice she deserves.'

Captain Callum Mills embraces Swans coach Dean Cox after winning the round 24 AFL match

Slater & Gordon lawyer Jackson Pannam said the firm has been asked by his client to determine if there was any basis for a civil claim

The team found the players had breached standards by staying out late, drinking and bringing women back to the Pullman East Melbourne hotel, near the MCG, early on Monday morning

A potential civil claim would be separate to any criminal proceedings.

None of the banned players had been interviewed by police as of Saturday morning, the Sydney Swans said in a statement.

However, a 'number of people have been spoken to' regarding the alleged assault, according to Victoria Police.

Carbone Lawyers partner John Karantzis said the two women he represented were suffering severe stress, anxiety and feared for their lives after online backlash from Sydney supporters over the affect of the incident on the Swans AFL season.

'There's a lot of interest in this case and they are literally in hiding and they are suffering,' he told Melbourne radio station 3AW on Friday.

'They want their voice to be heard,' Mr Karantzis said.

He was investigating a civil claim against the club in addition to individuals and said that the Swans hadn't been fully transparent as to who was involved and what had occurred.

He also said he understood that there were more than five people in the room.

The Swans have 'categorically' stated none of their staff were there and are not involved in the investigation.

The AFL's integrity unit is also investigating.

Sports.title: Manchester City agree £81.4m deal to sign Morocco's teenage World Cup star Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, after new boss Enzo Maresca insisted club urgently need a Rodri replacement
Sports.content:
Manchester City agree £81.4m deal to sign Morocco's teenage World Cup star Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, after new boss Enzo Maresca insisted club urgently need a Rodri replacement

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester City are set to complete the signing of Moroccan teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi for an initial £81.4million.

A breakthrough in protracted talks with Lille came in the hours before City’s Premier League season kicked off against Bournemouth, with City paying an initial £81m and an additional £4.3m in bonuses.

The Morocco international has been pulled out of their game with Angers today and is due to travel for his medical.

It provides a major boost for Enzo Maresca, whose side have looked light in midfield after the sale of Rodri to Barcelona and Bernardo Silva’s free transfer to Real Madrid.

City have now spent around £200m this summer and are expected to have a busy final week of the transfer window as they look to add more quality.

Maresca had suggested on Friday that he is looking for around 20 senior outfield players. Given that Omar Marmoush is heading to Tottenham and Newcastle United remain in discussions over Nico Gonzalez, there is an acute need for more bodies.

Ayyoub Bouaddi has been targeted by Man City to replace the gap left by Rodri's departure

Despite being only 18, Bouaddi has played almost a century of professional games and lit up the World Cup over the summer.

Lille had wanted to keep the midfielder for the campaign but City pushed for a deal that saw him join straight away. City are also closing on the £35m signing of Palmeiras winger Allan Elias.

Sports.title: Matthias Jaissle hits out at 'soft' penalty decision that cost Newcastle victory in 2-2 draw with Liverpool as Andoni Iraola backs £125m Alexander Isak after star's disappointing return
Sports.content:
Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle criticised the 'soft' decision to award Liverpool a 99th-minute penalty in their 2-2 draw, claiming that such officiating would lead to 'many penalties in the future'. The Reds, who had been unconvincing for much of the afternoon, rescued a point at the death when substitute Victor Munoz was brought down by Lewis Hall and Dominik Szoboszlai converted. But Jaissle did not agree with the award, as he said: 'I think you call it here a 'really soft one'. If you give that there will be so many penalties in the future. I'm not a fan of that, I have to say. I don't know if that is good for football. I disagree, but more I cannot say.' Newcastle led 2-1 thanks to goals from Anthony Elanga and Joe Willock - Cody Gakpo had equalised for the visitors - and they would have been deserved winners on a day of high emotion amid tributes to Kevin Keegan. 'In the end, I am a bit disappointed,' said Jaissle. 'But there is also some brightness, definitely, because the guys were doing an amazing job for over 90 minutes. We are a young squad and they really left their heart on the pitch and this is something we can build on. 'I'm proud. We are proud to see a unit on the pitch. The guys were trying to do it the intense way that we wanted to play. Front-footed, vertical in our approach. This, after such a short amount of time, I'm really happy. I felt the goosebumps straight away. You get energy from the stands and you just want to deliver it on the pitch. This synergy will be something special.' Liverpool rescued a point at Newcastle after the Reds were given a 'soft' late penalty Former Newcastle striker Alexander Isak endured a difficult afternoon and, after being booed every time he touched the ball, he skied the one good chance he had in the second half. New Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola said: 'I think he expected the atmosphere, so it was not a big surprise for him. He has tried everything, given us good positions on the ball, has had a couple of situations to finish in the box, but not the clearest. I value that he has continued pushing and fighting. It is a good step for Alex.' He added: 'We scored at the end so you probably have a better taste, but before the game we wouldn't have signed for this result.'
