Sports.title: Man City 2-1 Bournemouth: Enzo Maresca's bold call to play Marc Guehi in midfield was Pep Guardiola-esque - it paid off, but the Italian knows they need more signings there for a title challenge, writes JACK GAUGHAN
Sports.content:
Part of Manchester City's insistence on making this place an all-round entertainment venue is to install a zip line from the South Stand to the new one named after Pep Guardiola.

The general public will be able to fly over the pitch from one end of the Etihad to the other. Sounds adrenaline inducing but not quite as thrilling as the footballers balancing a high wire at the weekends instead. On the evidence of Enzo Maresca's Premier League bow, that is exactly what will be asked of them. No harness strapping these guys in.

Precarious, exhilarating, City wobbled, threatened to fall but ultimately stuck the walk with a bit of flourish and panache. Led by their greatest showman, Rayan Cherki, the engineer of both goals - including a sumptuous slid pass for Josko Gvardiol's stoppage-time winner.

Word around the team in recent weeks is that the Maresca era is going to be fun. He wants to go about attacking in a slightly different way to what became the norm to stunning success over the past decade and there were more than a few signs of that against a Bournemouth team showing no signs of an Andoni Iraola hangover.

For so long this felt like a false start with a squad that is offering more questions than answers at the moment and with critics circling on the back of last week's limp defeat by Arsenal. It does feel incomplete now and that will not change until more transfer business is completed.

Three players on the bench - Omar Marmoush, Nico Gonzalez and Jack Grealish - having more than a good chance of leaving before the window shuts is an eye opener. That Marc Guehi started and finished as a sitting midfielder, a role he has only ever performed twice in his professional career, was another.

Centre back Marc Guehi (centre) scored equalised for Manchester City during their 2-1 win vs Bournemouth after playing in the unfamiliar role of central midfield throughout the game

Josko Gvardiol netted a 91st-minute winner for City to complete their comeback victory

The gamble to play Guehi in midfield paid off for new City boss Enzo Maresca on Sunday

Yet had City lost this opener, as they appeared destined to do following Marcus Tavernier's 26th-minute goal, laying bare their defensive issues on the break, then Guehi would not have been the reason. Not even close, to be honest.

The sort of bold call that Maresca's predecessor, watching from the hills in Catalonia, would have been proud of: a head scratcher, a hotly-debated talking point on the concourse. An easy stick with which to beat the manager had this not ended up in late glory, Guehi having equalised from a Cherki corner six minutes from the end.

Guehi - who also missed a sitter from an Elliot Anderson set piece before the £116million midfielder went off injured - had showed deft feet and a good tactical understanding of the job at hand. Even so, his inclusion in that position showcased the work required before September 2.

With both Gonzalez and Mateo Kovacic on the bench, some will argue that Maresca was sending a message to the board. That doesn't quite stack up given a £81.4m move for Ayyoub Bouaddi was agreed with Lille hours before kick off. They will need one more in the engine room regardless, Enzo Fernandez at Chelsea the primary target, although that negotiation will be fraught.

'I always thought Marc could be a good midfielder,' Maresca said. 'It's not linked if we buy new players or not. You need to visualise it and then the last two days we tried him there in training. In the future when we need it, we now know he's going to be good in there.' Guehi joked that maybe he will be asked to play up front when he returns to Crystal Palace on Friday night.

Having watched the opening weeks of Maresca's reign, what has become clear is the need for physicality in central areas. Iraola's successor, Marco Rose, spoke of preying on mistakes in transitions, something that teams have always targeted in this stadium, and City will want more legs in there. Bouaddi offers that and it will be a prerequisite of whoever follows. There is unlikely to be enough depth without two new faces.

Conversations will be going on in the Manchester pubs about their right-back situation, too. When in midfield, Rico Lewis looked strong and knitted City together from pockets of space. When defending, he let Tavernier go for the goal and almost allowed Justin Kluivert to do exactly the same. Matheus Nunes improved City when coming on.

'I had the feeling that we had the momentum in the second half,' Rose said while ruing passive defending that allowed Guehi a free header six yards out and Cherki to later slip Gvardiol in for the sort of riotous finish witnessed so many times before at this ground.

'It's never done here. You know what you get. The quality of the team and this stadium. They know how to finish games.'

Marcus Tavernier wheels away in celebration after giving Bournemouth a first-half lead

Rayan Cherki started on the bench for City but Maresca has to find a spot for him in his line-up

MATCH FACTS AND RATINGS

Man City (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma 7; Lewis 5.5 (Nunes 57, 7), Khusanov 6.5, Dias 5.5, Gvardiol 7; Guehi 7.5, Anderson 7 (Kovacic 63, 6.5); Foden 6 (Grealish 82), O'Reilly 6.5 (Cherki 63, 8), Semenyo 6; Haaland 6.5 Subs not used: Rulli, Ait-Nouri, Gonzalez, Grealish, Marmoush, Reis Manager: Enzo Maresca 6.5 Bournemouth (4-3-3): Petrovic 6.5; Smith 6.5, Silva 6, Hill 7, Truffert 7; Scott 7.5, Cook 6.5 (Adams 75, 6), Kluivert 7 (Toth 75, 6); Rayan 7 (Gannon-Doak 87), Evanilson 6.5 (Jebbison 75, 6), Tavernier 7.5 Subs not used: Dennis, Diakite, Sanchez, Brooks, Rodriguez Manager: Marco Rose 6.5 Referee: Jarred Gillett 6

To finish it they turned to the finisher. On for 27 minutes, Cherki created more chances than anybody. He apparently wasn't given the nod to start because four others - Erling Haaland, Anderson, Guehi and Nico O'Reilly - are all effectively still in pre-season, according to their manager, and adding a fifth into the mix would negatively tip the scales.

'Rayan is quite a nice and clear boy, if he is not happy he wants to show it,' Maresca beamed. 'If he's next to me and he's not happy, you all realise that he is not happy because he is doing anything just to show that he is not happy. I know that he was not happy today but at the end I had to take a decision.

'His impact was unbelievable and he is that kind of player. What they have to do when they don't start is do what Rayan did today.'

The next order of business for Maresca, who understandably doesn't know his best XI - and a large part of that is so many of them being adept in a number of different positions - is to make sure Cherki is on the teamsheet. His sort of ingenuity, speed of thought in tight spaces, is exactly what City require by attempting to utilise a more high-octane way of breaking teams down.

He called this a work in progress and the positive aspect of that is if they keep winning matches while picking a way through then it will put them in a fine position to motor if things ultimately click. 'It has been a perfect day,' Maresca said after blowing kisses to the directors' box when Gvardiol's goal was ruled legal by VAR. 'It was quite emotional.'

High stakes and high wires. Maresca's City could well meet the entertainment criteria his bosses crave.

Sports.title: Aston Villa suffer NIGHTMARE start to the Premier League season as Unai Emery's side concede FOUR - and new signing is sent off - in opening half at Brighton
Sports.content:
Aston Villa suffer NIGHTMARE start to the Premier League season as Unai Emery's side concede FOUR - and new signing is sent off - in opening half at Brighton

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Aston Villa suffered the worst possible start to their Premier League campaign, conceding four goals and being reduced to ten men in the first half of their clash with Brighton at the Amex.

The Seagulls ran riot against Unai Emery's new-look Villans, netting four times in the opening 31 minutes to leave the Spaniard apoplectic on the touchline.

Villa's horror show started eight minutes in, after Maxim De Cuyper's effort smashed against the post before bouncing off centre-back Victor Lindelof and hitting the back of the net.

Ten minutes later, De Cuyper found the back of the net himself before Jack Hinshelwood netted a brace in less than two minutes on the half hour mark.

Emery was clearly enraged at his side's embarrassing start to the match, and could be seen going crazy once the fourth goal went in.

Aston Villa suffered a nightmare start to their opening Premier League game of the season against Brighton

The Seagulls shipped four goals past the hapless Villans inside just 31 minutes

Summer signing Joao Gomes was also sent off on his Premier League debut for Villa

'Unai Emery is steaming,' former Aston Villa star Lee Hendrie stated on Sky Sports. 'He hasn't had many days like this as Aston Villa boss. The amount of giveaways from Villa is extraordinary.'

But matters only got worse when debutant Joao Gomes lost his temper and kicked out at Georginio Rutter. Following a brief VAR check, the midfielder was shown a red card.

Brighton's first-half demolition of Villa was the fastest a team have raced into a 4-0 lead in their opening game of a season since Manchester United against Fulham in the 2006-07 season.

Alarm bells have been ringing at Villa Park during the summer due to the number of big names leaving the club.

Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne, and Ezri Konsa all started their Europa League triumph back in May but have moved on to pastures new.

Emery has brought in a host of new and exciting stars, such as Gomes, Johan Manzambi, Matteo Ruggeri and Zion Suzuki, which has brought some renewed optimism to the club ahead of the campaign.

However, that optimism dissipated rapidly after Villa's dismal opening 45 minutes at the Amex.

Sports.title: Newcastle 2-2 Liverpool: The Reds are as flawed and unpredictable as they were last term but their late equaliser already feels like a huge moment for Andoni Iraola, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
Newcastle 2-2 Liverpool: The Reds are as flawed and unpredictable as they were last term but their late equaliser already feels like a huge moment for Andoni Iraola, writes IAN LADYMAN

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

They came in their thousands to greet new dawns at Newcastle and at Liverpool and to pay homage to one of the greatest either club has ever known. The tribute to the late Kevin Keegan here at the place they call the Cathedral on the Hill before kick-off really was quite something.

Keegan - modest as he was - would have appreciated it but not as much as he would have a football match that ebbed and flowed dramatically and thrillingly and was not ultimately decided until almost the very last kick of the afternoon.

Newcastle - now under the guidance of German coach Matthias Jaissle - were as brave and energetic and committed as Keegan always liked his teams to be. At 2-1 up with only 30 seconds of added time remaining, they seemed to have this game won.

But Liverpool - as flawed and unpredictable here under Andoni Iraola as they were last season under Arne Slot - were admirably determined not to lose. And in the 96th minute, substitute Victor Munoz fell under a clumsy challenge from the otherwise excellent Lewis Hall and Dominik Szoboszlai smashed the resulting penalty high into the top corner with his right foot.

It felt like a huge moment in Iraola's early days. Defeat in game one would have weighed heavily. It was, however, the very most his team deserved.

On this evidence the problems the Spaniard has inherited from Slot will take a while to solve. Centre-forward Alexander Isak - booed throughout by Newcastle fans on his return to St James' Park - continued to look drained of any kind of belief or attacking instinct while Liverpool once again looked horribly vulnerable against a team able to break on them at speed.

Andoni Iraola will be relieved to see his Liverpool side escape with a point at Newcastle United

The Reds rescued a 2-2 draw thanks to Dominik Szoboszlai's (left) stoppage-time penalty

Szoboszlai rifled his spot-kick into the top left-hand corner to earn Liverpool an unlikely point

Newcastle, meanwhile, will wonder quite how they didn't win. Liverpool were comfortably dominant in possession but the better chances were Newcastle's and twice Yoane Wissa failed to convert very good opportunities with his team a goal to the good late in the game.

It is this that will keep Jaissle awake tonight. This really should have been a perfect start for the man chosen to succeed Eddie Howe.

Such has been the upheaval at the club over the summer that of the team that started a thriller lost 3-2 here to Liverpool almost exactly a year ago, only two players - Harvey Barnes and Anthony Elanga - were in the line-up for this one. There were three summer signings in the team and three on the bench but for long periods it was hard to tell.

Liverpool were skittish while Newcastle were resolute. Indeed the opening goal was utterly exhilarating while also having some Liverpool hesitancy written through it.

Ryan Gravenberch - one of his team's better players during last season's difficulties - did well to find space 25 yards from the Newcastle goal but as a shot at goal opened up for him, he for some reason chose to pass square to his left across the top of the penalty area. As soon as that pass was intercepted, Liverpool were in trouble.

Will Osula carried the ball out of his own half and released the galloping Elanga to his right. Liverpool left-back Milos Kerkez did his best to keep up with his opponent but it was a non-contest and with goalkeeper Alisson unwilling to advance beyond his six-yard line, Elanga was able to slide a low right-foot shot across goal and in to the far corner.

With only five minutes gone, the post Howe era on Tyneside was off to a flyer and for the remainder of the opening 45 minutes Newcastle were good for their lead.

Liverpool enjoyed some territory but it was a frenetic and broken game and when they were asked to defend Iraola's team looked every bit as uncomfortable and uncertain as they did last season.

Alexander Isak endured a difficult first return to St James' Park since leaving for Liverpool

Anthony Elanga (right) broke the deadlock early on with this brilliant finish for Newcastle

There were some glimmers of hope for Liverpool. A low Florian Wirtz shot from the left was saved by new Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek while there were two or three shots from decent positions that were blocked by home defenders happy to throw their bodies in the way of the ball when necessary.

On the whole, though, Liverpool lacked fluency with the right-sided combination of Jeremie Frimpong and young Rio Ngumoha struggling in particular to settle into an understanding. There was much fussing among the Liverpool fanbase last season about a perceived lack of game time for Ngumoha. Here, the 17-year-old - scorer of the winning goal in that game a year ago - got very little change out of the impressive Newcastle left-back Hall.

Up front Isak was largely anonymous. The Swede had smiled when jeered by the home fans during the warm-up but in truth looked a little cowed once the game started, seemingly low on confidence.

Early in the second half, Cody Gakpo seemed to have bailed his team out. The Dutch forward's low right foot shot when given too much space in the 55th minute flew like a rapier into the bottom corner. Briefly Liverpool looked set to take control, camping deep in Newcastle territory.

But another break from the home team did for them far too easily within a couple of minutes.

Cody Gakpo equalised for Liverpool after half-time with this long-range low strike

However, Newcastle soon hit back with Joe Willock finishing a superb counter-attacking move

Newcastle were outnumbered by six bodies to two as Wissa and substitute Joe Willock broke from their own half. But as the Liverpool players left the business of actually tackling anybody to each other, Wissa was able to feed his team-mate on the left side of the penalty area and Willock's curling right-foot shot found the net off the foot of Alisson's left hand post. It was a fabulous finish from the 27-year-old but at the same time another wretched goal for Liverpool to concede.

Liverpool needed a response but looked done for. Isak scooped a very good chance into the gods and would surely have been taken off had Iraola had any kind of alternative on the bench. And then came those two chances for Wissa, one missed at the near post from a low cross and another placed too close to Alisson when played clear.

That opportunity came and went with just five minutes remaining and didn't look to have cost his team by the time the Congo forward was substituted in the 95th minute. But time added for that switch actually gave Liverpool chance to launch one final attack and Hall's foul on Munoz was clear.

Liverpool are out of jail for now but Slot was sacked for a reason. Sustained recovery under Iraola could be a while coming.

Sports.title: Newcastle 2-2 Liverpool PLAYER RATINGS: Which Toon star was unplayable at times? And who delivered an anonymous performance at the start of a defining season?
Sports.content:
Newcastle 2-2 Liverpool PLAYER RATINGS: Which Toon star was unplayable at times? And who delivered an anonymous performance at the start of a defining season?

Dominik Szoboszlai scored a last-gasp penalty to earn his Liverpool team a draw at St James' Park in the first game of the Andoni Iraola era.

A raucous, hostile stadium was rocking after Anthony Elanga and substitute Joe Willock scored for Newcastle either side of Cody Gakpo levelling.

But Szoboszlai's 99th-minute thunderous strike from 12 yards saw Liverpool head back to Merseyside with a point that is hard to argue they deserved.

Alexander Isak was also back at his old workplace and was booed with his every touch. This is how Daily Mail Sport's Lewis Steele rated both sides.

Dominik Szoboszlai's last-gasp penalty rescued Liverpool a point at St James' Park

Newcastle (4-2-3-1)

Lukas Hornicek - 7

The Czech new boy signed from Braga started with a fine display which included a couple of strong stops to deny the likes of Wirtz and pantomime villain Isak.

Amar Dedic - 7

Another signing from Portugal, Austrian Dedic had a tough afternoon up against Gakpo and Kerkez on that side but stood tall.

Malick Thiaw - 7

The task was simple: keep Isak quiet. The Newcastle old boy barely had a sniff and all defenders could hold their heads high.

Sven Botman - 7

Made a last-ditch block to deny Munoz late on and, like defensive partner Thiaw, answered every question thrown his way.

Lewis Hall - 6

Was on for an eight out of 10 until the final seconds, when he gave away a stupid spot-kick. Did not need to foul Munoz and let his side down with a game-defining error.

Lewis Hall had a brilliant game - until he brought down Victor Munoz late on to gift Liverpool their penalty

Sean Steur - 6.5

Only 18, Steur is another who can be proud of his debut – though he was a bit slow at closing down Gakpo for Liverpool’s equaliser. The home side won the midfield battle.

Lewis Miley - 7

Newcastle fans were right to be worried about their midfield after losing Guimaraes and Tonali, plus an injury to Joelinton. But local lad Miley was excellent here.

Anthony Elanga - 7.5

Excellent run and finish for the first goal, with lightning quick pace the main weapon that undid Liverpool. Still had a lot to do but the shot was composed.

Yoane Wissa - 8.5

Like Isak, the man he replaced, Wissa had a first year to forget at his new club. But this was his best performance in a Newcastle shirt. Playing as a No 10, he was unplayable at times.

Yoane Wissa impressed after a difficult first season for Newcastle

Harvey Barnes - 7

Did a lot of dirty work off the ball that may go unnoticed. Asked questions of Frimpong throughout.

Will Osula - 7.5

A stellar assist for the opening goal and an accomplished performance overall. On a day when all eyes were on £125million Isak, Osula was the best No 9 on the pitch.

Substitutes:

Jacob Ramsey (for Steur, 56) - 7.5

Joe Willock (for Osula, 56) - 7.5

Jacob Murphy (for Elanga, 76)

Aladji Bamba (for Miley, 76)

Fabian Schar (for Wissa, 90+5)

Manager: Matthias Jaissle - 7.5

Got his tactics and substitutions spot on and what a way to introduce himself to the Premier League – nearly. Let down by Hall, who gave away a sloppy penalty.

New Toon boss Matthias Jaissle got his tactics spot on and was minutes away from a dream start to life in the Premier League

Liverpool (4-2-3-1)

Alisson - 7

Might be nit-picking but his positioning for Newcastle’s first goal was questionable. Could do little about the second and made some strong saves to keep his side alive..

Jeremie Frimpong - 5

Offered little going forward and was one of many players bypassed too easily for Willock’s goal in the second half.

Jeremy Jacquet - 6

Crisp passing on his Liverpool debut and made some OK tackles but maybe the experience of substitute Araujo would have been better at a hostile stadium like this.

Virgil van Dijk - 5

Slow at times and Liverpool struggled with passes in behind the back line.

Virgil van Dijk looked off the pace and struggled to deal with Newcastle's balls in behind

Milos Kerkez - 6

Outpaced for Newcastle’s opener. Was berated by team-mate Isak on 73 minutes when the Hungarian got a cross terribly wrong.

Dominik Szoboszlai - 7

A thunderous penalty to level it in the last second. Bailed out his team-mates who were poor overall. Where have we seen that before?

Ryan Gravenberch - 5

Whether by design or not, his forward runs left Liverpool exposed to the counter-attacks that led to Newcastle’s goals.

Rio Ngumoha - 6

Ten times better on the left flank. Played on the right here and was largely ineffective. Signing at least one new winger this week simply must happen.

Florian Wirtz - 4

Came close in the first half when Hornicek tipped his left-footed shot wide but otherwise this was an anonymous performance to start a defining season for Wirtz.

Cody Gakpo - 7

Stunning strike to equalise. Should have scored a second minutes later but took one touch too many. Has been heavily linked with Spurs but Gakpo was the best of Liverpool’s attackers here.

Cody Gakpo - linked with Tottenham all summer - drew Liverpool level with a stunning strike

Alexander Isak - 4

Got into some good areas and was let down by poor final balls from team-mates – but a day to forget for Isak on his return to Newcastle.

Substitutes:

Alexis Mac Allister (for Wirtz, 63) - 6

Victor Munoz (for Ngumoha, 63) - 6

Ronald Araujo (for Jacquet, 70) - 6

Lewis Koumas (for Gravenberch, 78)

Manager: Andoni Iraola - 6

Whether Liverpool had lost, drawn or even gone on to win, Iraola needs new signings this week if he is to realise his ambitions this year.

Referee: Stuart Attwell - 6

A bit trigger-happy with his cards early on but got the big decisions right.

Sports.title: Revealed: Terrorism threat could derail Manchester United's training ground expansion plans - INSIDE SPORT
Sports.content:
Revealed: Terrorism threat could derail Manchester United's training ground expansion plans - INSIDE SPORT

Manchester United could see plans to extend the life of a car park at its training ground thwarted - thanks to concerns over the potential for a terror attack.

The Premier League giants want to extend the life of a temporary facility they brought in for contractors to use during the £50m refurbishment works at the Carrington complex by a further three years.

However, Inside Sport understands that counter terrorism cops have evaluated the proposal – and police have ‘implored’ the club to increase security measures should their plans get the green light.

United have lodged a planning application with the local council and, as part of the process, Greater Manchester Police are entitled to have their say. Given the ‘high profile nature’ of the site, they have liaised with colleagues in Counter Terrorism who have assessed the situation.

In a subsequent message to the council, they note the lack of a secure entry and exit point for visitors. In what is a strong response, police say they ‘implore the application to provide suitable secure pedestrian access’ which would ensure that every visitor to the site will be vetted. They have also warned of the prospect of ‘bad actors’ entering the site among a group of pedestrians.

Man United's plans to expand Carrington have been thwarted by potential for a terrorist attack

And, in a move that will further increase headaches for Old Trafford bosses, the move has triggered a strong objection from locals. Action group Friends of Carrington Moss have set out their complaints over no fewer than four pages.

They say they are ‘particularly disappointed that United did not consider it necessary to consult with communities in advance of submission’ and claim that granting approval would increase car dependency in the area and is not an application for ‘sustainable development’.

The objection, which also brands United ‘shameful’ adds: ‘The applicant repeatedly states throughout its documentation that Manchester United is a world leading football club. It is clearly not world leading in sustainable operations.’ They also claim United removed two mature trees and ‘totally stripped’ other vegetation and say the car park was fully in use by March 2025 and not August, as had been suggested in planning application documentation.

Manchester United have been contacted for comment.

Jet-setting Gianni fights to hold onto power

When it comes to saving your skin, it would appear that saving the planet takes a back seat.

Flight logs seen by Inside Sport show that embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino, fighting for his highly lucrative job, is clocking up the air miles at a staggering rate of knots as he travels the world in an attempt to drum up support.

On Friday, his luxurious private jet – provided by FIFA sponsors Qatar Airways – left Doha for Rabat, where Infantino recently and infamously summoned officials for crisis talks. It then headed from Morocco to Punta Cana, in the Dominican Republic, where Infantino defied a request from one of his vice presidents to stay away from an Under 14 tournament in Punta Cana.

Victor Montagliani, the Canadian president of CONCACAF who many see as a potential successor, had asked the Swiss supremo not to visit amid concerns his presence would be a distraction from the event itself.

Under Infantino, FIFA provides the Caribbean Football Union with up to $5m from each four-year cycle and he may well have used the trip to remind officials of that point at a president’s meeting.

The following day, the same jet headed from Punta Cana to Paris. That is a total of around 11,800 miles at an estimated cost likely to run into the hundreds of thousands.

Gianni Infantino is unbothered about his carbon footprint as he clings onto power

'The Rest is F*** All'

There was huge noise earlier this year around Gary Lineker and his The Rest Is Football podcast after it signed a staggering deal with Netflix worth a reported £14m to produce a daily show throughout the World Cup. That deal has been extended for the next two seasons, with a promise of focus on the Premier League and Champions League in twice-weekly episodes from August.

However, the top flight’s big kick off came and went without as much as a peep, let alone a preview, leading some to joke about the longest World Cup holiday in the industry. Indeed, one insider mused: ‘It’s been noticeable on social media that nobody seems to be questioning where they are or demanding a new episode. The Rest Is Football? More like The Rest is F*** All.’

The silence from Gary Lineker's The Rest Is Football has not gone unnoticed

Spurs fan Kay-Jelski turns to North Londoners

Much has been said and written about changes to Match of the Day under BBC director of sport Alex Kay-Jelski. It has also not gone unnoticed that three of the four new arrivals – Robbie Keane, Toby Alderweireld and Thomas Frank have either played for or managed Kay-Jelski’s beloved Spurs, with some joking that we may be witnessing the boss’s ‘Tottenhamification’ of the iconic Saturday-night show.

EFL clubs stand firm on VAR

Do not expect to see VAR at EFL matches in the near future. Clubs have been spoken to about bringing the technology in for league games and have overwhelmingly decided to leave it to the play-off finals and Carabao Cup final (and all Premier League semis) with ‘significant opposition’ lodged. Football Video Support (FVS) has triggered a similar response, with an ‘overwhelming majority’ raising concerns over the FIFA-approved system which allows coaches a set number of ‘challenges’ to request a review of game-changing incidents.

Do expect an offer from Premier League clubs aimed at ending the deadlock over financial distribution to land across the EFL in the near future.

Sports.title: Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle claims late Liverpool penalty 'not good for football'
Sports.content:
Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle claims late Liverpool penalty 'not good for football'

Newcastle were denied three points when Liverpool scored a stoppage time penalty - but Matthias Jaissle has taken issue with the foul that was given against Lewis Hall

View 2 Images Matthias Jaissle was denied a statement win on his first Newcastle outing

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle was involved in a penalty row after Liverpool snatched a last-gasp draw at St James’ Park.

‌



Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai slammed home a 99th minute spot kick but Jaissle insisted referee Stuart Attwell should never have given the decision. Newcastle were denied a precious victory after Liverpool substitute Victor Munoz was brought down by Lewis Hall’s clumsy challenge.

‌



Jaissle said: “For me, it was no penalty - it was a really soft one. If you give that, we will see many, many penalties. I don't think that Lewis can do anything else, he cannot just disappear on the field! It’s a really soft penalty. If you give these penalties then you have to give a lot in this season and I’m not sure if that’s good for football.”

‌



Newcastle could have taken all three points as Liverpool striker Alexander Isak had a frustrating return to St James’ Park because his every touch was booed.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Jaissle praised Yoane Wissa but admitted the Newcastle striker could have won it. “It was an amazing performance - even if he could have killed the game! Their heads are a little down but we know we had many challenges, we're in a huge transition phase at the moment.”

‌



The Newcastle boss also admitted he wants more signings after a summer of change at St James’ Park. He added: “I hope so, today the lads were amazing, a young squad but we have some needs we know internally and we keep that internally. You can count them on one hand.”

Liverpool hero Szoboszlai insisted they showed their spirit under new boss Andoni Iraola - even if he admitted he could not hear himself think when he took the penalty.

View 2 Images Lewis Hall gave up a stoppage time penalty

‌



Szoboszlai said: “More than 50,000 fans in the stadium against you. You can't hear your own voice. That's why I love football and that's why I am doing it. We will never give up. I can guarantee you that. We have to fight every time - all day long for 90 minutes. Everybody who came off the bench also made an impact as well today. We need the whole squad and we need to be ready.”

Iraola admitted that Isak suffered amid the boos on his return but praised him and his team for carrying on fighting.

Iraola added: “I think he expected a little bit of the atmosphere. It’s not a big surprise for him, He has tried everything. He has given us good positions on the ball, probably has had a couple of situations to finish inside the box but probably not the clearest we wanted. But I value that he has continued pushing and fighting in the game and I think it was a good step for Alex.”

Sports.title: Alexander Isak was Toon Army's pantomime villain - but they'll never forgive his treachery
Sports.content:
Alexander Isak was Toon Army's pantomime villain - but they'll never forgive his treachery

NEWCASTLE 2-2 LIVERPOOL: Alexander Isak had the last laugh as Liverpool snatched a last-gasp point on Tyneside after he had been relentlessly booed for 90 minutes

View 3 Images Isak was relentlessly booed by Newcastle fans for 90 minutes (Image: Getty Images)

It was never going to end quietly.

‌



And on a stage made for heroes and villains, Dominik Szoboszlai rescued Liverpool in the 99th minute. As endings go, it was cruel and dramatic in equal measure.

‌



Szoboszlai crashed a penalty into the roof of the net before Liverpool’s players celebrated their smash-and-grab point with the travelling fans up in the gods at St James’ Park.

‌



For the second year running, Liverpool broke Newcastle hearts deep into added time as Rio Ngumoha snatched a 100th-minute winner last year.

This time, it was in the 99th minute with barely time for the restart which was so tough on Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle and his new-look team.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Newcastle have sold half the squad this summer, changed managers and yet they have not lost their soul or character because they fought and showed so much courage.

Twice Newcastle led and they revelled in making Alexander Isak the pantomime villain on his first return to St James’ Park. Nothing went Isak’s way.

The Toon Army booed Isak’s every touch and they will never forgive his treachery but in Jaissle they have found an inspirational leader.

‌



They scrapped, made life hard for the visitors and, for so long, it looked like Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola would get off to a losing start in his first game in charge.

Liverpool did look disjointed, the squad still needs a lot of work before the transfer window shuts and you can be certain they will be better in the weeks ahead.

View 3 Images Dominik Szoboszlai rescued Liverpool a point

‌



But whether Liverpool will be among the title challengers remains to be seen and may depend on their transfer business because they look short at the moment.

The bigger fear was for Newcastle after their mass exodus of all their big names and, after so many pre-match tributes for Kevin Keegan, you can be sure the late, great legend of both clubs would have been looking down enjoying such a dramatic game.

Newcastle could - and maybe should - have won but Liverpool stayed fighting until the end even if they were way below their best.

‌



It was loud, highly-charged and emotional even before kick-off and then erupted after just five minutes. Even in their wildest dreams, the Toon Army could not have expected such a dream start.

Liverpool midfielder Ryan Gravenberch charged forward, a shooting chance opened up but he overran the ball and allowed one of Newcastle’s army of new signings, Amar Dedic, to clear.

Newcastle forward Will Osula led the charge, he played in Anthony Elanga and the jet-heeled Sweden forward’s cross shot beat Liverpool keeper Alisson Becker.

‌



Liverpool came back and it took a sensational save from Newcastle’s new keeper Lukas Hornicek to keep out Florian Wirtz’s shot. The new signings are promising.

View 3 Images Joe Willock had fired Newcastle back in front in the second half

But Liverpool’s pressure was building. They levelled after half time. Gravenberch fed the ball into Cody Gakpo and the Liverpool forward arrowed a low shot into the bottom corner from outside the box. At that moment, Liverpool had the momentum.

‌



But Jaissle made two changes - Jacob Ramsey and Joe Willock came on - and, in keeping with everything else on his first day in charge, he proved himself to be a tactical genius. His enthusiasm is so infectious.

Newcastle forward Yoane Wissa led a brave counter attack, used all his strength to hold off Liverpool defenders and then fed Willock who scored with a low shot. The whole place erupted again.

Wissa had two chances to kill the game and make it 3-1. One was a sitter. And Liverpool just kept going and never gave up even if they lacked some quality in the final third.

Article continues below

Liverpool substitute Victor Munoz charged into the box. Newcastle defender Lewis Hall made a clumsy challenge. Referee Stuart Attwell pointed to the spot and Hall just hung his head in despair. Szoboszlai made no mistake.

Sports.title: Dominik Szoboszlai rescues last-gasp point for Liverpool at Newcastle - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Dominik Szoboszlai rescues last-gasp point for Liverpool at Newcastle - 5 talking points

NEWCASTLE UNITED 2-2 LIVERPOOL: Dominik Szoboszlai scored a stoppage time penalty to rescue a point for the Reds after Joe Willock's second-half strike looked poised to win the game for the hosts

View 4 Images Liverpool were rescued by Dominik Szoboszlai's penalty in stoppage time

Liverpool salvaged a point in the 99th minute as a Dominik Szoboszlai penalty ensured Newcastle's Matthias Jaissle era didn't start with a win at St James' Park.

‌



The Magpies were ahead inside five minutes thanks to Anthony Elanga's strike, his first for the club in the Premier League. They retained that lead going into half-time but Andoni Iraola's side came fighting back and Cody Gakpo fired home the visitors' equaliser on 55 minutes.

‌



Liverpool weren't level for long though as Joe Willock completed another counter attack to retake the lead. Newcastle looked set for three points but, just as there was stoppage time drama last year, Szoboszlai converted from 12 yards after Lewis Hall felled Victor Munoz.

‌



Newcastle broke with real pace to score the opener inside four minutes as William Osula ran at the Liverpool defence before sending Elanga clear, with the winger finishing impressively to ignited St James' Park.

Florian Wirtz forced Lukas Hornicek into a smart save as the Reds went in search of an equaliser, but that's as close as they would come in the opening 45 minutes with the hosts continuing to offer a threat in attack.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Liverpool would bring themselves back into the game when Gakpo fired home their equaliser. The Dutchman adopting a good position 25 yards out before receiving the ball in the space and firing home from range after being afforded time to take aim.

The Reds looked to have a spring in their step in the moments following their equaliser, but parity in the game only lasted three minutes. Newcastle again hit Liverpool on the counter with Yoane Wissa travelling half the pitch before finding Willock, who finished neatly.

The Magpies had almost completed their mission before Hall's foul gifted Liverpool a penalty deep into stoppage time, which Szoboszlai hammered into the roof of the net to rescue a point.

‌



Here's five talking points from the north east.

Not so doom and gloom for the Toon

After a summer that saw Newcastle cash in on three of their leading lights for more than £240million plenty have tipped the Magpies to have a season of struggle, especially after their change of manager midway through pre-season.

View 4 Images New boss Matthias Jaissle was denied the perfect start to life in Newcastle

‌



But Sunday's performance showed that this Newcastle side still have it in them to give it to the country's top teams. The St James' Park crowd also still believe and only need a bit of desire from their team to play their part from the stands. There's still much to like about the Newcastle game plan, even if they don't have the stellar names of years gone by. Had you gone into hiding over the summer and reappeared for the opening weekend, you wouldn't have known so much negativity had swirled about the Toon, but conceding so late will make Sunday's outing feel like a defeat.

Iraola learning scale of the job

Last season it was hard to gauge whether the title win of 2025 was the outlier or a fair reflection of where Liverpool should be, given they dropped to fifth last term.

That demise cost Arne Slot his job and Iraola was quickly bought in as his replacement. Results in pre-season, where the Merseysiders twice gave up two-goal leads to lose, exposed defensive flaws with the Spanish boss admitting the team weren't yet primed to play the style he demanded. Sunday was his first genuine chance to show what Iraola's Liverpool looked like, bar a ten minute spell to start the second-half and Gakpo's impressive outing, it looked set to end in defeat. Szoboszlai's penalty ensured the former Bournemouth boss doesn't begin with a defeat, but he did little more than clap, knowing mass improvement is needed.

‌



View 4 Images Joe Willock thought he'd score the winner in the second-half

Elanga the speedster

If there's one thing Newcastle lost when Anthony Gordon left for Barcelona it was out and out pace. But its easy to forget in Elanga they still have that outlet of raw speed, which proved crucial for the opening goal early on.

Elanga had a frustrating debut season at St James' Park, especially given he'd cost £55m, but he couldn't have began in better fashion. The winger only started 14 games in the league last year, appearing more often from the bench, but with the exodus of players his role will be magnified and he possesses the pace that Newcastle so often relied on when Gordon was in full flow.

‌



Isak's return

Last season when this fixture was played Isak was in the midst of trying to force his move from Newcastle to Liverpool and as a result was absent. He would eventually get his way, destroying the legacy he'd built in the north east, before enduring a wholly disappointing injury-hit campaign at Anfield.

View 4 Images Alexander Isak underwhelmed on his return to St James' Park

Sunday was Isak's first Liverpool-Newcastle clash as a Red and, inevitably, his every touch was booed by the home crowd. His every error or misplaced touch was roared even louder. His biggest chance came with 20 minutes remaining, but the Swede fired his effort well over to mark a forgettable first return. His Hungarian team-mate at least ensured he didn't leave having lost.

‌



The Wirtz problem continues

Last year didn't go to plan as Liverpool desperately tried to get the most out of the German, who was briefly the British record signing. He was played from the flanks and centrally. Iraola decided that Wirtz's best role was at the heart of the attack.

But on the hour mark, and with Liverpool needing a goal, the Reds boss chose to hook his playmaker. A damning verdict and the camera was quick to pan to the former Bayer Leverkusen man, who looked unimpressed as he took his spot on the bench. Liverpool's investment in Wirtz means they have to persevere with him, but the weight on his shoulders is only increasing.

Sports.title: English cricket hit by fresh scandal as star handcuffed after nightclub incident
Sports.content:
English cricket hit by fresh scandal as star handcuffed after nightclub incident

Videos have circulated on social media of England cricket star Brydon Carse being led away by police in Derby with the ECB having now spoken out on the incident in the aftermath

View 2 Images The ECB have confirmed that they have launched an investigation (Image: Getty Images)

The ECB have confirmed that they have launched an investigation into a video that appears to show England star Brydon Carse being put in handcuffs by police.

‌



Carse, 31, was shown being placed into cuffs by officers on a night out in Derby following Durham's County Championship win over Derbyshire. The incident showed the fast bowler being surrounded by four police officers and restrained.

‌



Durham and England team-mate Matthew Potts is seemingly attempting to speak with Carse, while former England Test captain Ben Stokes can also be seen nearby. As per The Telegraph, Carse was briefly detained by officers but was not formally arrested and returned to the team hotel.

‌



Nevertheless, the ECB have confirmed that they are taking a close look at the incident. A statement read: "We are aware of an incident which is reported to have taken place in Derby last night, and are currently investigating. We will provide a further update when possible."

Carse was part of the England squad for the first Test against Pakistan, but was not selected. Depending on the investigation, he could return to contention for the second Test beginning at Lord's on Thursday.

‌



Carse took two wickets for Durham against Derbyshire, with Stokes claiming five of his own. Several members of the Durham squad then went out in Derby city centre that evening, which is when the alleged incident is thought to have taken place.

View 2 Images Brydon Carse was handcuffed by police in Derby on Saturday

The incident follows Stokes and Gus Atkinson being stood down following a nightclub incident after England's first Test win over New Zealand earlier this summer. The duo missed the second Test but returned for the third, during which Stokes announced his international retirement.

Article continues below

Joe Root, who has returned as England Test captain, has confirmed the team will no longer be subject to the controversial curfew that Stokes and Atkinson were said to have breached.

Carse has 14 Test caps and 44 white-ball appearances for his country. He featured in all five Tests in the Ashes in Australia over the winter, finishing as England's leading wicket taker.

Sports.title: DAVID YATES: Juddmonte International 'mess' should have been investigated
Sports.content:
The Mirror Racing postbag is seldom empty, but the postie got a particularly good workout in the wake of the Juddmonte International at York on Wednesday.

A few of you got in touch because I managed to tip Item – stopped clocks, and all that – many more wrote to lament that the race, as a spectacle, was a mess and the remainder wanted to talk about Action.

Was this a case of team tactics - but with the aim of hindering an opponent rather than helping a team-mate?

Most of us expected Action would be on pacemaking duties for Constitution River, but instead he spent the early furlongs of the race at the back of the eight-runner field than at the front of it.

‌



Overhead footage showed him directly on the outside of Constitution River’s market rival - and 5-6 favourite - Ombudsman, whom William Buick sought to make his ground on the inside rather than sweeping round the outer, as has been his wont.

View 2 Images Dave Yates - Chief Racing Correspondent at Daily Mirror

Personally, I don’t think it affected the result. Perhaps, as Ombudsman’s joint-trainer John Gosden suggested, the rain had made life difficult for the market leader, or maybe - for some other reason - the five-year-old just wasn’t at his best.

But the thrust of your correspondence is that the stewards, at the very least, should have held an inquiry into Action’s running and riding – and I’m in full agreement.

‌



In the race of the season, as in any other, justice must not only be done but manifestly and undoubtedly be seen to be done.

ITV Racing play politics

Ebenezer Scrooge hoped the visit of Jacob Marley’s ghost was a hallucination triggered by an undigested bit of beef, a blot of mustard, a crumb of cheese or a fragment of an underdone potato.

I desperately felt the same after ITV Racing’s opener to the York coverage on Wednesday, when Ed Chamberlin had somehow become Prime Minister and was addressing the nation.

‌



But it was all true. Too horribly true.

Non-runner madness

Benvenuto Cellini. The can of worms that keeps on giving.

Since the Epsom stewards declared the Derby favourite a non-runner because he had a foot on the running board of his stall, hardly a week goes by without a similar case going the other way.

‌



On Wednesday, Native Instinct got his nose wedged between the gates after he anticipated the start. He sustained a swollen gum and a cut, but still goes down as a runner. Madness.

Is racing popular?: You bet

The Saturday of York’s Ebor Festival brings to an end the English summer’s marquee meetings.

The combined crowds across 14 days at Royal Ascot, Glorious Goodwood and York is bearing down on 500,000 people. They were there to watch the horseracing, and to bet. Are you listening, Mr Burnham?

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca dodges early Man City question as late show spares his blushes
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca dodges early Man City question as late show spares his blushes

MANCHESTER CITY 2-1: BOURNEMOUTH: Enzo Maresca was facing an embarrassing defeat on his first Manchester City outing before two late goals as the Italian seeks to fill the huge void left by Pep Guardiola

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca's Man City tenure began with a win

Had Pep Guardiola masterminded this comeback win, he would have been hailed a genius again. But Enzo Maresca still has a long, long way to go before earning comparisons to the bloke he has replaced.

‌



In the meantime, Maresca will just be relieved to have got his first positive result on the board, however difficult it was to get. For more than 84 minutes Manchester City appeared to be heading towards the kind of defeat which would have raised serious questions about Maresca's ability to fill the gigantic shoes of Guardiola.

‌



Marcus Tavernier had put Bournemouth ahead before half time, sending most of the Etihad into silence. And despite dominating possession, City offered little in the way of a fightback, aside from some bad misses from Erling Haaland and Marc Guehi.

‌



But thanks to bit of luck and the introduction of Rayan Cherki, Maresca's men somehow snatched victory from the jaws of defeat. Guehi's deflected header from Cherki's corner levelled the scores, before Cherki's clever pass allowed Josko Gvardiol to snatch the winner in stoppage time. And breathe, Enzo.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Fresh off a thrashing from Arsenal in the Community Shield, City begun their league campaign knowing the visit of Bournemouth carried a bit more significance. Starting with a home defeat to a team you'd trounced by an aggregate score of 34-6 in nine previous home wins, was unthinkable.

‌



Not least when Maresca had rolled the dice and picked two of his stars in unorthodox positions, with Guehi operating as a defensive midfielder and Nico O'Reilly starting in the No.10 role. Visiting boss Marco Rose was also starting a new job, and handed a debut to Antonio Silva following his arrival from Benfica.

City started well and ripped into Bournemouth. Haaland tore through midfield to help create a chance for Rico Lewis, but his shot was well saved by Dorde Petrovic. O'Reilly had a free header from the resulting corner, but sent it onto the roof of the net, before Phil Foden had a shot blocked.

View 2 Images Josko Gvardiol scored in stoppage time to down Bournemouth

‌



Haaland then blew a golden chance, fluffing a cross from O'Reilly after the England international had charged half the length of the field before picking him out to perfection. The blunder looked even worse on 26 minutes, when Rose's men went ahead.

It was their first real attack of the game, but a clinical one. City failed to deal with a long ball forward, allowing Rayan to turn sharply and pick out Evanilson, who delivered a sublime cross which Tavernier converted at the back post. Cue silence in most parts of the ground.

It took a crucial interception from Gvardiol to stop Rayan from having a clear run on goal, as City continued to wobble. Petrovic scrambled to his left to keep out a header from Haaland, but the visitors were looking the most dangerous. Tavernier curled a strike just wide and Gianluigi Donnarumma did well to deny Justin Kluivert.

‌



A rumpus on the stroke of half time summed up City's frustrations. That feeling got worse when Guehi missed an absolute sitter from close range, when it looked easier to score.

City needed a spark and Guehi provided one, equalising with five minutes remaining to make amends, before Gvardiol completed the fightback. But it could still promise to be a long season for Maresca. Provided he survives to the end of it, of course.

Sports.title: Newcastle pay touching tribute to late Kevin Keegan alongside Liverpool as family thank club
Sports.content:
Newcastle pay touching tribute to late Kevin Keegan alongside Liverpool as family thank club

Newcastle United and Liverpool paid tribute to the late Kevin Keegan ahead of their Premier League clash at St James' Park on Sunday, with the family of the legendary manager giving their thanks

View 5 Images Tributes were shown to Kevin Keegan in Newcastle (Image: Sky Sports)

Newcastle United gave an emotional tribute to the late Kevin Keegan at St James' Park on Sunday afternoon ahead of their Premier League opener with Liverpool. The legendary former footballer and manager died at the age of 75 last month following a battle with cancer, with tributes pouring in across the world of sport.

‌



And given the Armthorpe-born icon represented the Magpies both as a player and a manager, as well as Liverpool during his playing days, the clubs felt it was only right that they afforded him an emotional send-off ahead of their first English top flight outing of 2026/27.

‌



On top of the players warming up in shirts adorned with Keegan's iconic number seven, 500 shirts were laid in a mosaic reading 'legend' and 'There's only one Kevin Keegan,' in the centre circle of the stadium. Bobby Moncur, Ian Rush, Shola Ameobi and Sir Kenny Dalglish also laid wreaths in the Newcastle memorial gardens ahead of Sunday's 4.30pm kick-off on Tyneside.

‌



Kevin Keegan's cause of death as Liverpool and Newcastle prepare to pay tribute READ MORE :

A letter from Keegan's family was also included in the pre-match programme, in which fans were thanked for their support over an incredibly tough period. It read: "Dear Newcastle United fans and the incredible city of Newcastle.

"The past couple of weeks have been some of the hardest that our family has endured, saying goodbye to our husband, father, and grandfather, Kevin. Despite living outside of the region, your love and warmth from the North East has reached our hearts and filled us with so much comfort during these difficult days.

"The empathy, compassion and warmth of this extraordinary club and community have shone through; the outpouring of love has been truly overwhelming. Having seen the tributes outside St. James’ Park, members of our family came home to Newcastle to see the memorials in person.

‌



"The sea of black and white shirts and scarves, alongside colours from so many other clubs, reminded us how much Kevin meant to the footballing world. It was a sombre moment that reminded us of our pain and loss, yet matched with immense pride and love as we read so many personal and heartfelt messages.

View 5 Images Former Newcastle and Liverpool players laid wreathes (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

"Kevin always shared his love for Newcastle United, Geordies, and the city, captivating us with stories told with his infectious smile. Seeing these tributes brought those stories to life for Kevin’s grandchildren, showing them how deeply their grandfather was loved in return.

‌



"It also allowed us a quiet moment to reflect on many fond memories of Kevin’s incredible career and the incomparable bond he shared with Newcastle. Your football club, city, and community show a passion that truly embodied Kevin as a footballer, manager, and family man.

"We will be eternally grateful for the adoration and strength you have given our family when we needed it most. Newcastle, thank you for your love. The Keegan Family."

Placards were also left on seats around St James' Park for fans to hold up in the build-up to kick-off, adorned with instructions and the words "Long live the king." Wor Flags also provided a display of Keegan's name in red in the Liverpool section of Level Seven, while the number seven sat below among the home fans.

‌



View 5 Images Placards were left for fans inside St James' Park (Image: Getty Images)

The Newcastle-based organisation also erected a one-off tifo which showed a collage of Keegan from his time at Newcastle United as both a player and a manager, as well as the words "King Kev." Meanwhile, fans held banners in the stands, showing Keegan's iconic "we should all be dreamers message."

A minute of applause was also given for Keegan as kick-off fast approached, with both sets of supporters, as well as the likes od Dalglish and Alan Shearer joining in. A two-time Ballon d'Or winner, Keegan kicked off his footballing career at Scunthorpe United in 1968, spending three years with the club before a move to Liverpool arrived.

‌



View 5 Images Newcastle and Liverpool fans paid tribute to Keegan (Image: Sky Sports)

After spending six years with the Reds, he moved onto Hamburger SV, before returning to English soil with Southampton in 1980. Keegan arrived at St James' Park in 2982, enjoying a two-year stint with the club before seeing out the last year of his career at Blacktown City.

In a trophy-laden playing career, Keegan won the First Division title with Liverpool three times, as well as the European Cup and a pair of UEFA Cups. He also won a Bundesliga title with Hamburg. Keegan then stepped into the world of management in 1992 with Newcastle, guiding the club to a First Division (now Championship) title in his maiden season.

‌



View 5 Images Keegan was a club legend for Newcastle and Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

After five years at the helm, Keegan moved onto Fulham for two years, and enjoyed short stints with England and Manchester City before one last dance with the Magpies in 2008.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
