Sports.title: F1 Dutch GP red-flagged after Verstappen crash
Sports.content:
Formula 1's Dutch Grand Prix has been red-flagged after one lap following an enormous accident for home hero Max Verstappen.

At the end of lap 1 on a damp circuit, Verstappen lost control of his Red Bull as he tagged the white line on the inside of Zandvoort's final turn - the banked, flat out Luyendyk corner leading onto the main straight.

Verstappen veered head on into the outside wall, before his car crossed the track and came to a standstill on the inside.

The Dutchman soon reported he was OK and apologised to his team for ending his race early.

Verstappen was fortunate not to be collected by any other cars, with Alpine's Pierre Gasly taking avoiding action, while in the background Audi's Nico Hulkenberg also narrowly avoided a huge accident as his team-mate Gabriel Bortoleto spun in front of him.

Under the red flag all drivers gathered in the pitlane awaiting the restart. They were having to navigate a field of debris before pit entry, but teams are allowed to change tyres under a red flag ahead of the restart. That restart is expected at 15:33 local time.

Max Verstappen Photo by: Anni Graf - Formula 1 via Getty Images

At the time Verstappen was running seventh after a disappointing qualifying session. Polesitter Lando Norris retained his lead during a chaotic start sequence, with championship leader Kimi Antonelli passing George Russell for second.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc gaining two positions to hold down fourth ahead of the second McLaren of Oscar Piastri and team-mate Lewis Hamilton.

For Verstappen, the accident marks an unfortunate end to a six-year spell racing on home soil, winning the first three editions of the Dutch Grand prix revival in 2021, 2022 and 2023. The race will disappear from the calendar after organisers decided not to pursue a contract renewal with F1 management.

Earlier in the week, the four-time world champion announced he had extended his Red Bull contract until the end of the 2030 season.

Sports.title: Wolff jokes that Mercedes already has Verstappen for the "real hero races"
Sports.content:
As is tradition, Mercedes organises a special media session with Wolff and representatives of the Dutch press at Zandvoort. In recent years, those roundtables have often produced some eye-catching comments, much to the amusement of Mercedes team members as well.

Two years ago at Zandvoort, for example, Wolff more or less confirmed Kimi Antonelli's F1 promotion, even though the formal announcement was not scheduled until a week later at Monza.

Last year, Wolff spoke openly about the talks with Verstappen over a potential move to Mercedes and caused some surprise when the subject turned to several AI-generated pictures of the pair. Wolff also joked about AI-generated images of himself and Verstappen, including explicit deepfakes circulating online.

At the start of this year’s conversation, Wolff clearly still remembered all those moments and laughed: “You know, let me get into the groove and then I'll give you a few punchlines!”

Dacia, Verstappen and "hero races" at the Nordschleife

#3 Mercedes-AMG Team Verstappen Racing, Mercedes AMG GT3 EVO: Max Verstappen, Daniel Juncadella, Jules Gounon, Lucas Auer Photo by: Red Bull Content Pool

Wolff then addressed Verstappen’s new Red Bull deal. According to the Mercedes team principal, the chances of a move were greater last year than they have been over the past few months, something that already became clear in the spring.

During last year’s Dutch media session, Wolff said he felt their paths would cross at some point. Asked by Autosport whether Verstappen’s new Red Bull contract has definitively changed that feeling, Wolff clarified that, in his view, their paths are already crossing – just not in F1.

“Well, the paths have crossed already with the GT racing. I think when we jointly developed that programme a year and a half ago it seemed a long shot,” Wolff said. “It seemed to be a long shot because could Red Bull ever allow Max in a Mercedes GT3?

“But they were open-minded and we are thankful for that because the project has been a success, the Red Bull Mercedes project. We have this joint cooperation between the two brands and Max, and it is nice to see that it’s successful.”

#3 Mercedes-AMG Team Verstappen Racing, Mercedes AMG GT3 EVO: Max Verstappen, Daniel Juncadella, Jules Gounon, Lucas Auer Photo by: Qian Jun / MB Media / Getty Images

Wolff then joked that Mercedes therefore gets Verstappen for what he considers the “real hero races” — the endurance events on the Nordschleife, with the Nurburgring 24 Hours as the absolute highlight.

“Exactly! You know, we have these things here in F1 with massive gravel traps and flat run-off zones. The real racing is where you go through the trees and up and downs over crests and blind corners. And against the Dacia!”

With those final words, Wolff is referring to Olli’s Garage Racing, which competes with a Dacia Logan in the iconic 24-hour race in the Green Hell.

After mentioning the Dacia, Wolff immediately turned to the press officer present, telling him that Mercedes should invite the Dacia crew to an actual F1 Grand Prix.

“No, seriously, they are heroes!” Wolff laughed. All of those things contribute to the magic of the Nordschleife, with Wolff enjoying seeing Verstappen behind the wheel of the Winward Mercedes-AMG GT3.

“You race against 150 cars on the Nordschleife in day and night, fog and rain, and ice. So obviously none of these races are 24 hours, but those are the real hero races.”

Could Verstappen ever get the same freedom at Mercedes?

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Mark Thompson / Getty Images

Whether Verstappen and Wolff’s paths will ever cross in F1 is something the latter does not dare to predict, if only because nobody knows what the driver market will look like in two or three years’ time.

“And what the future holds, I don't know, but the mindset is what I have just said. I don't know where the paths are going to cross. Will it be in karting, will it be in GTs, or will it be in F1 or some other joint projects in the future?

“I think that may happen one day, but maybe not necessarily with Max in a Mercedes Formula 1 car.”

The latter may not be necessary either, now that Mercedes already has its star of the future in Kimi Antonelli.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images

Another question is whether Verstappen would receive the same freedom to pursue outside racing projects at another F1 team.

“I think every team is different, but I think what I am trying to do is to identify what it is that makes the driver fast within our structure.

“What kind of framework do we need to provide to extract the best performance of the driver, and part of that is obviously the well-being. And that is something that I am very keen on as well.”

Sports.title: Verstappen suffering from "flu-like" illness as Zandvoort exposes Red Bull's fundamental problems
Sports.content:
With three victories since the Dutch Grand Prix returned to the calendar in 2021, Max Verstappen can already look back on a very successful period. The final edition in 2026 has proven an ordeal so far, both in terms of Red Bull’s pace and Verstappen’s physical condition.

"I've felt better before, yes," Verstappen admitted during the Dutch media session in the paddock after qualifying. "I feel a bit flu-like and I’m just not feeling as much energy as normal."

Asked whether that also affects his performance behind the wheel, he continued: "No, I don’t think so. I think once you’re in the car, it’s actually fine."

It does mean Verstappen is experiencing his final home race somewhat differently and is mainly looking forward to the moment he can get some rest: "Of course I still enjoy all the fans in the grandstands, but apart from that, I’m mostly looking forward to getting some sleep."

Why Zandvoort exposes some fundamental Red Bull problems

Aside from Verstappen’s physical condition, Red Bull is also struggling for performance at the circuit in the dunes. The home hero had to settle for seventh on the grid and was more than four tenths behind polesitter Lando Norris in qualifying.

"We changed quite a lot on the car after the sprint, but none of it made any difference," Verstappen said when asked by Autosport.

According to Verstappen, the Zandvoort circuit exposes some of Red Bull’s weaknesses to an exaggerated degree Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

"The balance of the car is the biggest problem. It’s just not consistent throughout the entire corner, but it has been like that all season. It’s just a little worse at some circuits than at others."

In that respect, Zandvoort is a track that exposes the RB22’s weaknesses more than most.

"It depends on the tarmac sometimes, but also on the layout of the track. This one is for sure not our best layout, but we just need to work on it. We can guess on what track it might be a little bit better, but we need to try and just dial it out."

Verstappen added that, in his view, it is not so much related to set-up, as Red Bull has tried everything in that respect: "I think we’re now simply more limited by some fundamental problems with the car that we need to solve.

"At this circuit you also have some fast corners and we’re lacking there as well. In general, if you don’t have a good balance, you can’t really attack the corners. And if you don’t have traction either, you can’t get out of the corners properly, so all of that costs time."

It means Verstappen considers seventh place the maximum achievable result on Sunday under normal circumstances, particularly if there is no chaos caused by rain.

Without rain, Verstappen reckons that P7 will be the best he can hope for in his final home race Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

It may not be the Zandvoort farewell he had hoped for, although the four-time world champion stresses that the Dutch GP era as a whole has already been a great success.

"It’s absolutely the end of an era," he said. "To have had your own home race and to have been able to win it a few times is very special. Of course, it’s a shame that it’s going away, but on the other hand, it has also given me a lot of great moments and memories."

Whether another memorable moment will be added remains to be seen, but Verstappen took a pragmatic view in conclusion.

"I’m really only satisfied when we win, but that’s going to be very difficult tomorrow," he said. "We’ve been a little too slow throughout this season and that’s not suddenly going to change in Zandvoort, but we’re just going to try to enjoy it one last time."

Sports.title: Russell defends “fair” decision to let Antonelli into second place | Formula 1
Sports.content:
George Russell said letting his team mate and championship rival overtake him was the correct decision which minimised the risk to their races.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli ran ahead of Russell until he made an extra pit stop during a late Virtual Safety Car period. When Antonelli closed on Russell afterwards, Mercedes ordered the pair to swap positions.

Russell complied, though it handed Antonelli a six-point swing in the championship fight between the pair of them. That erased the gain Russell made in the previous day’s sprint race.

However Russell said letting his team mate by was the correct thing to do for Mercedes.

“We’ve always said as a team, when we’re on different strategies, we’re never going to fight and we’re always going to invert, and that’s always just been our rules,” he explained.

“The fact is Kimi was ahead of me before the VSC and he tried something different to protect us as a team. He kind of copy-pasted what the Ferraris did.”

Although Russell believes there was a chance he could have successfully defended his position from Antonelli – as he later did with Lewis Hamilton, thanks partly to the timing of another VSC period – he also said trying to defend could have compromised his race.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“Could I have kept him behind? Maybe. But equally it could have been a P5 as well. So, in the end, you know, he deserved to be P2. I think P3 was a fair result for me.”

Russell fell behind Antonelli at the start of the race, then got stuck behind Oscar Piastri and never managed to get back on terms with his team mate. “It was tough,” he said.

“The first VSC came at a pretty awkward timing for me because I felt really strong on the hard [tyre]. I think Kimi’s and my race was kind of the opposite. I had a tough medium stint, he had a very strong medium stint, then I had a strong hard stint, he was struggling.

“But that VSC gave Lewis a free pit stop and obviously Kimi pitted as well. And from there on in, I knew I was going to be under threat.

“I was managing enough in the high-speed corners to allow me to be fast in sector three and defending into turn one [Tarzan]. So I was pleased with that performance.”

Sports.title: Antonelli says extra pit stop “put George at risk” too | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli was not convinced his extra pit stop in the Dutch Grand Prix was the right decision as it risked compromising his race.

The Mercedes driver made an extra pit stop 16 laps from the end of the race, taking advantage of a late Virtual Safety Car period. It dropped him from second place to third behind his team mate George Russell

Antonelli was able to repass his team mate for second place after Mercedes ordered Russell to let him through. However Antonelli was unable to gain on race leader Lando Norris.

Afterwards Antonelli said the strategy call had unnecessarily risked both their races, even though he had been struggling on his previous set of tyres.

“It was a difficult second half for me, especially in the last stint on the hards,” he said. “I was just really struggling. I had little confidence in the car and it was not easy.

“Then obviously we pitted [under the VSC] and also that was a bit tricky. But then also George, I have to thank him because he made my life a lot easier.

“But I still think probably we could have stayed out and gone until the end with the same set [of tyres] because it put us a little bit at risk. Also, I feel we put George at risk with having to let me by and everything.”

Although he led most of the race, Antonelli said he was unlikely to win it. “I still think, at the end of the day, it was a great team execution with how things were,” he said. “”I think today [second place] was the maximum we could have done because the pace of the McLarens, especially in the second half, was just too strong.”

“It was a good ending of a difficult weekend for me where I struggled with the feeling of the car, did a lot of mistakes on my side – sprint quali, quali, also in today’s race with Lando I could have defended a bit better,” he added. “So for sure there were things that I didn’t do well this weekend, and for sure the feeling wasn’t as good.”

Sports.title: “We weren’t unlucky”: Hamilton tells Ferrari their tactics cost him third place | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton told Ferrari they cost him a chance to finish third by failing to use team orders during the Dutch Grand Prix.

He finished fourth behind George Russell after losing time earlier in the race when he caught team mate Charles Leclerc. Hamilton repeatedly urged Ferrari to tell Leclerc to let him through, but the team instead to chose wait a lap and then bring the leading Ferrari into the pits.

“Let’s not hold ourselves up from an potentially better result,” Hamilton told the team when he caught Leclerc.

After spending a lap behind Leclerc, Hamilton warned Ferrari “we’re just losing time.” Once Leclerc came in, Hamilton sarcastically remarked: “Big waste of time guys, good job.”

Hamilton’s attempt to pass Russell at the end of the race was thwarted when the Virtual Safety Car was deployed. After he finished fourth race engineer Carlos Santi told Hamilton: “Thank you Lewis, was a bit unlucky with Russell.”

“We weren’t unlucky,” Hamilton replied, “we lost time earlier on and that cost us P3.”

“We can discuss it offline,” he added.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Hamilton explained his frustration after the race, pointing out Mercedes did not hesitate to swap the order of their two drivers when it benefitted them overall.

“I want to win,” said Hamilton. “I’m here to win and it is difficult when you’re looking ahead and you see the two Mercedes drivers, they get the call and it’s done and they execute straight away.

“They let Kimi by and let him get on with the race. I was on a different strategy and it was not the same here.

“That’s a little bit difficult but we just have to take it, we’ll take it off line. When I go back now, I’ll speak to them about it.”

Sports.title: Williams pair apologise for crash: ‘It’s not a Verstappen-Ricciardo Baku situation’ | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Both Williams drivers apologised for their roles in the collision between the pair during the Dutch Grand Prix.

However the stewards ruled Carlos Sainz Jnr was responsible for the collision which ended his team mate Alexander Albon’s race.

The collision occured as Albon tried to overtake Sainz on the outside entering Tarzan corner. Sainz locked up and made contact with the other Williams.

“It was a situation of the race put us with Alex on a fresher medium [tyre] behind,” Sainz explained. “I was struggling already a lot with my hard tyres there towards the end of the race and all of a sudden when I went to defend, a big bump in the braking area into turn one surprised me.

“I triggered a massive front lock and without wanting, obviously, I took Alex with me, which is the last thing you want to do with a team mate. But honestly I was caught off guard with that big bump there in the braking and triggered a massive front lock that I couldn’t recover later.

“So apologies for that and we will move on as a team. I think it’s just not the position we want to be in.”

The stewards handed Sainz a 10-second time penalty, ruling he “locked up and caused a collision between both cars” and was “wholly at fault”.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

However Albon also apologised for his role in the collision. He said it was not as serious as other clashes between team mates, notably the 2018 collision between Red Bull duo Max Verstappen and Daniel Ricciardo at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix which took both drivers out.

“It’s not good for the team,” said Albon. “Obviously we apologise to the team, but it’s not a Verstappen-Ricciardo Baku situation.

“We’ll review it for sure but I think he maybe just locked up and I tried to avoid it as well but we had damage so we had to retire.”

Sports.title: Hulkenberg explains how he avoided team mate Bortoleto in “scary” near-miss | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Nico Hulkenberg described how he made an “instinctive” last-second swerve to avoid T-boning his team mate in the Dutch Grand Prix.

Gabriel Bortoleto overtook Hulkenberg moments before spinning in front of him on the first lap of the Dutch Grand Prix.

“It was scary, sketchy,” said Hulkenberg. “You’re a passenger to some [extent].”

Bortoleto lost control of his car in the final corner, moments after Max Verstappen did the same and hit the barrier on the outside. Bortoleto kept his car on track but Hulkenberg had to make an immediate call whether to swerve to the left or right of the other Audi.

“I tried to react as late as possible and then just instinctively chose the side,” Hulkenberg explained. “Obviously I was waiting to see if he’s going to slide up or down. On a wet track it’s sketchy and difficult, but luckily we managed to avoid that.”

Bortoleto suspected he lost control of his car partly because he saw Verstappen going off ahead of him.

“I just saw big smoke coming out,” he said. “I think it was Max that crashed and then I maybe made a small reaction on the steering.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“But I just felt something and then I also lost the car. I did a 360, came back.”

Both Audi drivers finished the race, Hulkenberg claiming points for eighth while Bortoleto’s poor start and spin left him 13th. Bortoleto said he had other “issues” in his race but was unwilling to elaborate on them.

“I don’t want to go too much into details, because I don’t know if I can say, or whatever. But we just need to understand some stuff that happened today, and we’ll move on.

“I had a few start problems today that almost made me not probably manage to run out of the grid box, but I appreciate the work of the team. They were really on it to make it happen and to fix everything.

“It’s a shame the result was not what we wanted today, but Nico scored some points, so that’s good. We brought some points for the team at home, so good.”

Sports.title: Colapinto claims penalty for overtaking under yellow flags was “very harsh” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Franco Colapinto committed two yellow flag infringements during the Dutch Grand Prix and was given penalty points on his licence for each.

Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad were also penalised for failing to obey F1’s yellow flag rules.

Colapinto’s first penalty was for overtaking Yuki Tsunoda as they passed double waved yellow flags on the first lap of the race. The flags were shown in response to Max Verstappen’s crash at the final corner, which littered the track with debris, as well as Gabriel Bortoleto’s 360-degree spin at the same corner.

“Car 43 [Colapinto] was behind car 22 [Tsunoda] entering turn 14 and overtook car 22 in the double yellow flag sector before the [finishing] line at the end of lap one,” the stewards noted.

“Normally such infringement requires a 10 second stop[-and-]go penalty, but the stewards acknowledge the complications caused by the significant amount of debris on track at this point and take this into account as mitigating circumstances.”

The stewards issued the same decision regarding Arvid Lindblad who overtook Pierre Gasly at the same time. Both Colapinto and Lindblad received drive-through penalties and two penalty points on their licences.

Colapinto was already gaining on Tsunoda as they rounded the final corner when Verstappen crashed ahead of them. He continued to pass the Racing Bulls as the crash unfolded ahead of them.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

The Alpine driver criticised the stewards’ decision, calling it a “very harsh penalty” which “Colapinto: compromised the whole of our race”.

“It’s quite tricky, I think, to manage those situations when there is a car and pieces of car everywhere flying around and you have to make a decision,” he explained. “It was clearly much more dangerous to slam on the brakes in the middle of the straight and on the water and on the banking and not doing what I’ve done.

“I guess the rules are written [this way] but it should be much more flexible and give a little bit more, not just consistency, but a bit of flexibility in different situations that you can clearly see that this shouldn’t be penalised exactly what the rules say. But in the end of the day we still lead an infringement.”

Colapinto received another penalty point, and a 10-second time penalty, for failing to slow sufficiently for yellow flags later in the race when Esteban Ocon retired. The stewards noted he “passed a single yellow flag without discernibly reducing speed although also

receiving a visible warning on the dash.”

“As the infringement was not considered dangerous or egregious, a penalty on the lower end of the available scale is imposed,” they added. They also found Liam Lawson guilty of the same infraction and issued the same penalty.

The decisions leave Colapinto on a total of four penalty points, Lawson on three and Lindblad on two.

Sports.title: Putting Moses Itauma Behind A Paywall Hurts His Future
Sports.content:
Fans are being asked to pay to watch an unproven 21-year-old headline against an opponent who is respected within boxing but has little drawing power. A bare-bones undercard filled with domestic-level scrubs going nowhere gives undecided buyers zero reason to order the event.

Thin Card Leaves Itauma Carrying The Show

Sam Noakes against former WBO lightweight champion Denys Berinchyk is the strongest supporting fight. Constantin Ursu meets Ben Vaughan, Aloys Junior takes on 40-year-old Mike Perez, and Guido Vianello faces Moses Jolly.

Those fights may serve their purpose on a regular DAZN card, but this is a premium broadcast. None carries enough public interest to take pressure off Itauma and Hrgovic.

The promoters are trying to collect star-level money before Itauma has become a star. That strategy reduces the number of people who will see him and makes it harder for him to develop the support required to sell future events.

Exposure Should Come Before PPV

Regular cards should remain Itauma’s home until he is at least 26 and has been shown repeatedly to boxing fans. Five more years of accessible fights would let viewers follow his development, learn his personality, and become invested in his career.

Anthony Joshua became a major attraction because millions of British viewers watched his early fights. Itauma is being denied that broad introduction by a business model that demands payment without first establishing a connection with the public.

An IBF title would give Itauma a belt, but it would not automatically make him an attraction. Hiding him behind a paywall may bring in money on August 29. It also means fewer people will be watching when he takes the most important step of his career.

Sports.title: Hearn Claims TKO Paid For Tyson Fury Story Reposts
Sports.content:
“Firstly, that’s a plant,” Hearn said after revealing that BoxingScene reporter Lance Pugmire had contacted him about an email he received. “It was sent by TKO to journalists. I actually was told by a number of people that they’re financially incentivizing people to repost Tyson Fury’s story of him trying to spin the narrative. It’s absolutely wild what’s going on.”

Hearn then disputed how the circulated document had been presented.

“The email that was sent was an email between Matchroom and Sela detailing outstanding points that we want resolved. The addendum that was sent to Sela regarding the changes that we want to the contract if you want to do the fight in the US did not have one of those things from that leaked email in.”

Selective Leak or Paid Campaign?

At least two media outlets obtained the disputed information. Hearn named Pugmire, while The Sun stated that it was among several media organizations given the material. No complete list of recipients has been made public.

That reinforces Hearn’s contention that the email was circulated selectively, though it falls well short of proving that reporters received financial incentives. Providing favorable information to selected reporters is a familiar tactic during a contentious negotiation. Pugmire’s possession of the material only shows that someone wanted its contents made public. It does not reveal who sent it directly or establish that money changed hands.

The distinction between the email and the addendum is also central to Hearn’s defense. He maintains that the leaked correspondence covered unresolved business between Matchroom and Sela, while the addendum contained separate terms required for moving Joshua vs Fury from Britain to the United States.

Until Hearn produces evidence, the alleged paid media campaign remains hearsay. Obtaining a leaked document is not proof that a reporter was rewarded for publicizing it.

Sports.title: Julian Jackson vs Gerald McClellan: Five Rounds of Violence
Sports.content:
Seven years younger, McClellan arrived from Emanuel Steward’s Kronk Gym with a 27-2 record and 26 knockouts. The challenger attacked with the speed, aggression, and confidence of a fighter who did not expect his opponents to survive long.

This was more than a meeting of knockout artists. Jackson had to prove that his experience and single-punch power remained enough to stop a younger destroyer. McClellan needed to show that his quick victories had prepared him for a champion who punched harder than anyone he had faced.

Jackson Tests McClellan’s Chin

McClellan struck first, hurting Jackson with a right hand during the opening round. The champion recovered and began landing hard punches to the body in the second. A heavy left hook downstairs hurt McClellan and forced him to retreat. Jackson kept attacking the body in the third, using feints to slow the challenger’s aggression and create openings for his wider punches.

An accidental clash of heads left Jackson bleeding and resulted in a point deduction from McClellan under WBC rules. Jackson already had a history of eye trouble, making the damage especially concerning.

After four rounds, two judges had Jackson leading 38-37, while the third had the fight even at 38-38.

Low Blows Trigger a Brutal Finish

Two low punches from Jackson interrupted the fifth. McClellan went down after the second and received time to recover, giving the champion a brief pause after several physically punishing rounds.

The break had the opposite effect. Once Mills Lane restarted the fight, McClellan drove a right hand into Jackson’s head and followed with left hooks that sent the champion onto his back. Jackson somehow rose, but his bloody face and unstable legs showed how badly he had been shaken. Another attack dropped him a second time. Lane stopped the fight at 2:09 without allowing Jackson another chance to continue.

The stoppage earned The Ring magazine’s 1993 Knockout of the Year award. McClellan won their rematch by first-round knockout one year later, but the original fight remains the more revealing contest.

Jackson showed that McClellan could be hurt, yet hurting him was not enough. After recovering from the low blow, the challenger turned a close middleweight fight into a violent ending within seconds.

Sports.title: Xander Zayas Faces Dangerous Road At Middleweight
Sports.content:
That is an ambitious schedule for a 23-year-old coming off a seventh-round stoppage. Ennis dropped Zayas three times and took control once he began applying steady pressure. The additional six pounds will not erase what happened or give Zayas the punching power needed to hold off natural middleweights.

Power was never one of his strengths at junior middleweight. He scored 13 knockouts in his first 23 victories, often relying on combinations and movement rather than ending fights with one shot. His punches may carry even less authority against opponents accustomed to taking shots from 160-pound fighters.

Careful matchmaking will be necessary if Top Rank intends to get Zayas into a championship fight before the end of 2027. Yoenli Hernandez would be an especially difficult opponent because of his size, activity and strength.

None of the current champions offers an easy opening. Carlos Adames brings the pressure and power that gave Zayas trouble against Ennis. Aaron McKenna is physically strong and willing to fight at a high pace. Erislandy Lara remains a skilled counterpuncher despite his age, while Denzel Bentley has enough size and power to punish mistakes.

A ranked opponent who allows Zayas to settle into the new division can be found for February. Getting him from that bout to a title opportunity without crossing one of the division’s most dangerous fighters will be the difficult part.

He may feel better at 160, but comfort alone will not make him stronger, more durable, or harder to pressure. His middleweight campaign will depend as much on opponent selection as improvement.

Sports.title: Jack Catterall Blocks Teofimo Lopez’s Three-Unification Plan
Sports.content:
“180 days @WBABoxing which means November ✅ I understand the politics of boxing better than most. Rolly had a voluntary; now it’s time for my shot! No ducks, no more swerving. Me v Teo next,” said Catterall on X.

His message also answered Teofimo’s intention to pursue three consecutive unification matches without making a mandatory defense. Such a schedule would leave no room for Catterall and require the WBA to ignore or alter its previous ruling.

Romero was elevated to Super champion before Catterall defeated Shakhram Giyasov for the WBA’s secondary welterweight title on May 23. The WBA ordered the Super champion to face the winner within a maximum of 180 days, placing the deadline in November.

One voluntary defense has already been granted. Romero used it against Teofimo rather than facing Catterall, and the British southpaw does not believe the new champion should receive another exception.

A fight with the winner of Ryan Garcia versus Conor Benn is Teofimo’s preferred next step, and he has discussed collecting the remaining welterweight belts. Those matches involve more money than a Catterall defense, which explains his preference. Still, taking Romero’s belt also meant inheriting the obligation attached to it.

This is not merely a request for consideration. Catterall holds the secondary belt and has a WBA directive supporting his demand. If the organization enforces its own ruling, three straight unification fights will have to wait.

Teofimo Lopez Wants Three Unifications Without Facing One Mandatory

Teofimo Lopez believes his DAZN contract will take him directly from one welterweight unification to another without stopping for a mandatory defense of his WBA title.

The newly crowned champion is targeting Liam Paro, the winner of Ryan Garcia versus Conor Benn, and eventually Devin Haney. If Lopez gets his way, every appearance during the rest of his deal will involve another champion.

During his post-fight press conference, Lopez said:

“I got three fights with DAZN, and all of them are the road to undisputed. We’re going right to every world title. We’re not taking no title defense, no nothing. Whoever’s next, we’re going for him.”

A unification technically includes a defense of the belts involved, but Lopez’s meaning was clear. He does not plan to face an ordinary mandatory or ranked challenger between attempts to collect the other titles. If that plan proceeds, it will consume well over a year. Each fight requires negotiations between promoters, networks and boxing organizations before the participants complete training camps and recover afterward. Lopez also left the Romero fight with a cut over his right eyebrow that may delay his return.

The first unification depends on another event. Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn are scheduled to fight on September 12, after which the winner will need time to recover and negotiate with Lopez. The next stage against Liam Paro or Devin Haney requires another lengthy round of discussions.

Completing all three fights may leave contenders in several organizations waiting 12 to 18 months. Some will be forced into additional bouts to protect their rankings while the champion moves from one financially attractive unification to another.

Unifications often receive priority because reducing the number of champions is supposed to benefit boxing. That principle becomes difficult to defend when it is used repeatedly to prevent every other challenger from receiving an opportunity.

Granting one exception for a major fight is understandable. Three consecutive exceptions create a separate set of rules for the boxer who generates the most money. Ranked contenders must keep winning while Teofimo remains protected from facing any of them.

The strategy also depends on Lopez winning every fight. A loss transfers the collected titles to another champion, who may then request additional exceptions for more lucrative bouts. The waiting challengers must begin the same process again with someone new.

The schedule Teofimo described requires approval from more than DAZN. The WBA and the other organizations must authorize each step. If they permit three straight unifications without requiring a mandatory defense, the “road to undisputed” will become another example of boxing’s business interests overriding its competitive structure.

Sports.title: Rolly Romero Demands Teofimo Lopez Rematch
Sports.content:
Romero’s argument rests largely on who landed the punches that did the most damage.

He produced the fight’s clearest breakthrough in round five. Romero cut Lopez over the right eye, then hurt him with a left hook and looping right before pressing forward looking for the finish.

Lopez weathered it. Romero never found the final punch.

That distinction ultimately proved costly.

Romero disputed the scoring immediately afterward and dismissed the idea that Lopez had seriously troubled him.

“I got hit with two punches the whole fight that barely grazed me. I was never in any trouble. When I heard 114-114 I knew it was a robbery.”

The numbers tell another part of the fight.

CompuBox credited Lopez with a 124-73 advantage in total punches landed. His jab supplied much of that difference, connecting 62 times for a career high while Romero failed to land double-digit punches in every round except the fifth.

Lopez’s feet also forced Romero to continually rebuild his position before punching. Once Lopez recovered from the fifth, he spent longer stretches dictating the distance rather than exchanging where Romero carried the greater threat.

Romero still found him again.

A left hook late in the 11th knocked Lopez off balance and gave Romero another strong moment entering the championship round. He could not produce enough consistent work around those breakthroughs to convince two judges.

Lopez described his approach in simpler terms afterward.

“I just had to stay busy and keep my range against a strong puncher. I’m just looking forward to the next thing.”

That is the argument Romero now has to live with. He landed some of the night’s most damaging punches, while Lopez banked rounds with the jab, movement and higher output.

Romero had the openings to take the verdict out of the judges’ hands. He hurt Lopez in the fifth and caught him again in the 11th, but neither attack became a finish. Against a fighter banking rounds behind 62 landed jabs, isolated power shots leave too much arithmetic for three judges.

Sports.title: Hearn Says Anthony Joshua Contract Has Already Been Breached
Sports.content:
“What they want to do is they want to pay Anthony Joshua less money because that’s how it will work out with the difference in location. They want him to do a load of additional stuff. I’m not going to blow things up, which I could do so easily, but there has been breaches in AJ’s contract already which we’ve let slide because these guys are our partners and our friends, or were,” said Hearn.

Correcting “are” to “were” when describing the organizers as friends shows how badly the relationship has deteriorated. Hearn’s position is that Joshua signed for a British event and cannot be blamed for refusing to accept less money and additional duties merely because the preferred location changed.

Much of his anger was directed at a leaked Matchroom email containing a list of unresolved issues. Hearn believes it was deliberately circulated to journalists and falsely presented as Joshua’s demands for agreeing to fight in America.

None of the items in that email were included in the addendum Matchroom submitted for the proposed US move, he said. In Hearn’s view, the leak was intended to support Fury’s accusation that Joshua and Matchroom were being greedy and holding up the fight.

There were also claims that some people were financially encouraged to repost Fury’s version of events. Hearn offered no evidence during the press conference, so that allegation remains entirely his account. Still, anyone reading an alleged list of new demands without knowing it came from a separate email would naturally conclude that Joshua was asking for more.

The dispute extends to Dana White. Hearn says the agreement excludes TKO and Zuffa from promoting the event, despite White publicly identifying himself as its promoter. Nick Khan contacted Hearn about finding a way for TKO to participate, but White’s public approach had damaged those talks.

Time is nearly gone. The coming week was described as the deadline for preserving the proposed November date. Netflix needs time to promote the event, while Madison Square Garden may release the date and book something else. Joshua remains committed to fighting Fury, but the argument over location, money, and promotional control must be resolved within days.

Sports.title: Catterall Threatens Teofimo Lopez’s Big-Money Welterweight Plans
Sports.content:
A majority decision over Rolando Romero at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas gave Lopez the belt. His steady pressure, jab and body work earned scores of 116-112 and 115-113, while the third judge returned a 114-114 card.

Watching from outside the ring, Catterall made his opinion clear on social media.

“I beat either of these pair no doubt in my mind,” said Catterall on X about Teofimo and Rolly.

That confidence is not difficult to understand after Lopez’s welterweight debut. Romero spent long stretches moving backward and waiting for one power counter. His low output allowed Lopez to win rounds through activity without producing a dominant offensive performance.

When Romero finally attacked in the fifth, he hurt Teofimo with a left hand and opened a cut over his right eyebrow. Lopez recovered and regained control, but he never seriously hurt Romero despite landing the cleaner punches for much of the fight.

A more difficult test comes from Catterall. The British southpaw will not concede as many quiet rounds. His timing, counters and disciplined defense can disrupt Teofimo’s lead hand and force him to reset before attacking. He also has the patience to punish the wide punches Teofimo throws when he becomes frustrated.

The WBA ordered its Super champion to face the winner of Jack Catterall vs. Shakhram Giyasov within 180 days of their May 23 bout. Catterall won that fight and holds the secondary WBA welterweight title, placing him next in line for a consolidation bout. The period ends on November 19, although the WBA has not issued a new public order naming Lopez since he defeated Romero. The original WBA ruling established the timetable.

The cut over Lopez’s right eyebrow may delay the consolidation fight. November 19 is less than three months away, leaving limited time for the wound to heal before he resumes sparring and completes another camp. His team can request a medical extension if contact training places the cut at risk of reopening. Any added time would only postpone the obligation unless Catterall accepts a step-aside agreement or the WBA grants Lopez permission to take another fight. That delay may allow Lopez’s team to pursue Garcia, Benn or Haney.

Less money and greater risk make Catterall an opponent Teofimo has little reason to welcome. Based on Saturday’s performance, Lopez will need more than steady pressure and a busy jab against a disciplined southpaw who will make him pay for every mistake.

Ghana News.title: Adamus welcomes 12-month roadmap to revive mine, restore investor confidence
Ghana News.content:
Adamus Resources Limited has welcomed the government’s decision to develop a 12-month roadmap to resolve challenges surrounding the company and restore the Adamus mine to sustainable operations.

The company described the outcome of a recent meeting at the Presidency as a “significant and constructive step forward” towards securing the future of the mine and protecting the interests of its employees, contractors, suppliers, host communities and other stakeholders.

Under the agreed framework, Adamus Resources, the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources and the Minerals Commission will jointly develop the 12-month turnaround roadmap.

A six-member management team, comprising three representatives from Adamus and three from the government, will oversee the implementation of the programme.

In a statement, Adamus said the collaborative approach would allow all parties to focus on restoring the mine while protecting its value to Ghana and stakeholders.

“Adamus remains committed to the future of the mine,” the company said.

It assured employees, contractors, suppliers, host communities, business partners, investors and the Ghanaian public that it understood the uncertainty and anxiety caused by developments in recent months.

The company said the mine plays an important role in supporting livelihoods, businesses and communities in the Western Region, while contributing to Ghana’s mining sector and the wider national economy.

It therefore urged its employees, contractors, suppliers and host communities to remain calm and supportive as the agreed process unfolds.

Adamus said it would continue engaging with the government and relevant institutions and provide updates as the turnaround process progresses.

The company expressed confidence that the challenges confronting the mine could be resolved through cooperation among the government, Adamus, employees, financiers, suppliers and host communities.

Roadmap to be presented within two weeks

According to Adamus, the next key milestone is the presentation of the 12-month turnaround roadmap to the Presidency within the agreed two-week period.

The company described the process as more than an effort to resolve a dispute, saying it is intended to protect an important Ghanaian asset, preserve jobs and livelihoods, restore confidence and create conditions for a viable and productive future for the mine.

Adamus thanked the government, the Presidency, the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources and the Minerals Commission for their willingness to engage towards a resolution.

It also expressed appreciation to its employees, host communities, suppliers, financial partners and the Ghanaian public for their patience and continued support.

“Adamus Resources Limited remains committed to working with all stakeholders to turn this opportunity into a successful turnaround, a stronger future for the mine and restore confidence in the Ghana mining industry,” the statement said.

Ghana News.title: T-bills: Government records 162% oversubscription, interest rates slump
Ghana News.content:
The government recorded an astonishing 162% oversubscription of the treasury bills sales.

According to auction results by the Bank of Ghana, most of the investors bought the 364-day bill because of its high yield.

The government accepted about GH¢5.8 billion of the total bids.

The 364-day bill was once again the most subscribed bill as GH¢9.9 billion of the bids were tendered, representing 183% of the total bids.

The uptake was, however, GH¢2.6 billion.

The 182-day bill received bids of GH¢1.2 billion. A little above GH¢766 million was accepted.

For the 91-day bill, GH¢3.1 billion of the bids were tendered. A little above GH¢2.4 billion of the bids were accepted.

Meanwhile, interest rates continued to dip on the yield curve.

The yield on the 91-day bill went up by 39 basis points to 5.07%.

That of the 182-day bill also decreased to 7.08% from the previous week’s 7.27%.

Similarly, the yield on the 364-day surged by 91 basis points to 11.59%.

Ghana News.title: UPSA moves to turn student research into market-ready solutions
Ghana News.content:
The University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA) is intensifying efforts to bridge the gap between academia and industry by transforming student research into practical solutions to real-world problems.

The initiative is part of a broader innovation and creativity drive led by UPSA Vice-Chancellor, Prof. John Kwaku Mensah Mawutor, to ensure that academic research does not remain confined to university shelves but contributes to solving problems in society.

Speaking at the UPSA Innovation Day Cohort programme, Prof. Mawutor said universities had long been criticised for producing research that rarely translates into practical solutions.

“Our main objective is to move research from the shelves to the market,” he said.

“As we all know, universities, particularly at the undergraduate level, usually introduce students to basic research. We teach them how to conduct research, but at the end of the day, their work often remains on the shelves.”

He said the situation had also discouraged some students from undertaking research because they could not see its practical impact.

Pairing disciplines to solve real problems

Prof. Mawutor said UPSA introduced an interdisciplinary model last year under which students from different academic programmes collaborate to develop practical solutions.

“Instead of allowing an accounting student to conduct research solely in accounting or taxation, for instance, we now require every accounting student to work with an information technology student,” he explained.

He said research findings from one discipline could then be transformed into digital products by students from another discipline.

He cited a team of accounting students that developed a tax solution which, after collaboration with IT students, was transformed into a digital tool that could help taxpayers assess their tax obligations.

“These are the kinds of solutions we need in today’s world. Everything we are doing is geared towards solving real problems,” he said.

‘Ghanaians are naturally innovative’

Responding to concerns about the level of innovation in Ghanaian universities, Prof. Mawutor said the challenge was not a lack of talent but the absence of adequate platforms and opportunities for students to demonstrate their abilities.

“Ghanaians are naturally innovative. Once someone decides to attend a university, it shows that the person wants to acquire knowledge.

“We must provide students with platforms and environments that allow them to become more innovative,” he said.

He said students were now encouraged to engage with companies, communities and individuals to identify real problems and develop practical solutions.

One example, he said, was a facility-booking platform developed by students to allow users to check venue availability, make bookings and pay online without physically visiting the campus.

“That is innovation. If we underestimate these students and fail to provide them with the right platforms, they will never have the opportunity to demonstrate their abilities,” he said.

‘We want to produce millionaires before graduation’

Addressing concerns that thousands of graduates leave Ghanaian universities each year without the practical skills required to solve national problems, Prof. Mawutor said UPSA was determined to contribute to changing the situation.

“We must start somewhere. We must stimulate their innovative potential for the benefit of Ghana,” he said.

He said the university wanted to expand the way it celebrates student achievement at future congregations by recognising entrepreneurial accomplishments alongside academic excellence.

“We often celebrate academic performance, but in the coming years, whenever we hold our congregations, we want to celebrate not only academic excellence but also entrepreneurial achievements,” he said.

“We want to produce millionaires before they graduate. That is the dream, and it will come to pass.”

Prof. Mawutor said UPSA management would also work to connect student innovators with potential investors.

He disclosed that one participant in the innovation cohort had already secured employment through the initiative.

Developing locally relevant research

The Vice-Chancellor also said faculty members were being encouraged to develop theories and teaching materials that reflect Ghanaian realities.

He cited the university’s Book Ownership Project, which encourages lecturers to develop teaching materials using familiar local examples, such as Melcom, rather than relying predominantly on examples from foreign markets.

“Next year, you will see many theories being developed and propounded by our lecturers here. You will see bigger and better innovations,” he said.

The initiative forms part of UPSA’s broader effort to make university education more practical, entrepreneurial and responsive to the needs of industry and society.

Ghana News.title: NDC Volta team tracks development projects across four districts
Ghana News.content:
The Volta Regional Communication team of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) has undertaken a monitoring exercise across four districts of the Volta Region to assess the status of ongoing and completed development projects in education, health, roads, markets and other sectors.

The exercise covered the Agortime-Ziope, Ketu South, Ketu North and Anloga districts, where the team inspected dozens of projects at various stages of implementation.

According to a statement issued by the Volta Regional Communication Officer of the NDC, Kafui Agbleze, the exercise was intended to provide regional and constituency communication teams with first-hand information on government interventions, verify the status of projects and improve communication on their expected impact on communities.

Mr Agbleze, his deputy, Del Bright and constituency communication officers were joined by members of the respective constituency communication teams during the monitoring exercise.

Agortime-Ziope

In the Agortime-Ziope District, the team inspected projects in the education, health and economic infrastructure sectors, including completed facilities, ongoing projects and projects described by the party as legacy interventions.

In education, a three-unit classroom block with an office and store at Adzorvi and a two-unit classroom block with ancillary facilities at Takuve have been completed.

A three-unit classroom block with an office and store at Obemla has reached the roofing stage, while another three-unit classroom block with an office and store at Akpokope was identified as a legacy project.

The team also inspected three health projects, including a Community-based Health Planning and Services (CHPS) compound with semi-detached nurses' quarters at Datsiedu, which has reached the roofing stage.

Another CHPS compound with semi-detached accommodation for three nurses at AGOSEC Top in Kpetoe is also at the roofing stage, while a CHPS compound with nurses' quarters at Agorhokpo, described as a legacy project, has been completed.

The team further visited the constituency's 24-Hour Economy market, which is under construction.

According to the Regional Communication team, the market is intended to expand economic opportunities, improve trading infrastructure and provide a more conducive environment for traders and businesses in the constituency.

Ketu South

In Ketu South, attention was drawn to the ongoing Phase II of the Blekusu Sea Defence Project, which is intended to protect coastal communities that have suffered repeated tidal wave destruction and seawater intrusion.

According to the NDC communication team, the project has already resulted in the reclamation of several kilometres of land, while some areas previously affected by seawater entering homes have experienced relief from the problem.

The team said residents who interacted with its members expressed satisfaction with the progress of the project and the protection it was providing to affected communities.

The reclaimed land is expected to be used for social amenities and other facilities for communities along the affected coastline.

Other projects inspected in Ketu South included the ongoing Tokor-Ho Road project and a 24-hour Economy market under construction.

The team also identified a proposed modern market at Aflao, which was yet to commence at the time of the monitoring exercise.

In education, six-unit classroom blocks at Avoeme Basic School and Akaglakorpe have been completed, while a vocational training centre has also been completed.

A CHPS compound and nurses' quarters at Dogbekope were under construction.

The communication team said regular monitoring was important in promoting accountability and transparency while ensuring that the public received accurate information on the progress and impact of development projects.

Ketu North

The monitoring exercise in Ketu North identified a significant concentration of projects in the education sector, alongside health and public service infrastructure.

Among the education projects inspected was a six-unit classroom block with an office and store at Tadzewu.

At Afife Senior High School, the team inspected boys' and girls' dormitories as well as a one-storey classroom block and a 20-seater toilet facility for male and female students.

Other projects included a three-unit classroom block at Koeyiborkope, being undertaken in collaboration with Pencils of Promise, and a dormitory facility at Dzosec.

The team also inspected a kindergarten block at Fiagbedu School in Dzodze, and six-unit classroom blocks at Tove-Dzodze, Deme-Dzodze and Ehi.

At Kave-Dzodze, another kindergarten block is being constructed in collaboration with Pencils of Promise.

Six-unit classroom blocks at Tsiyinu, Afife, and Afife RC Basic School were also among the education infrastructure inspected.

In the health sector, the team visited a CHPS compound with staff quarters at Adzoatsi and another CHPS compound at Tsiyinu in Afife.

The newly constructed National Health Insurance Scheme office at Dzodze was also inspected as part of the public service infrastructure component of the exercise.

The Regional Communication team said the projects were expected to improve teaching and learning conditions, expand access to primary healthcare and strengthen the delivery of public services in the constituency.

It said the monitoring formed part of efforts to equip communication officers with information on projects being undertaken under President John Dramani Mahama's "Resetting Agenda".

Anloga District

In the Anlo Constituency, the Regional Communication team and its constituency counterparts identified 16 projects covering education, health, accommodation, roads and sports infrastructure.

The education projects included the construction of a two-unit kindergarten block with ancillary facilities at Tegbi and a Science Laboratory Complex at Anlo Senior High School (ANSECO).

The proposed science facility comprises six specialised laboratories, offices and storerooms covering Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Agriculture, Integrated Science and Information and Communication Technology.

Another two-unit kindergarten classroom block was identified at ANSECO, while the team also inspected the re-roofing of a six-classroom block at Agorve.

Other education infrastructure included a three-unit classroom block at Akplorwotorkor and another three-unit classroom block at Sodzi.

In the health sector, projects included the construction of a CHPS compound at Agorve, the provision of a Free Primary Healthcare Container at Srorgboe and the construction of a CHPS compound with a two-bedroom nurses' bungalow at Dzita.

Accommodation projects inspected included a teachers' bungalow at ANSECO comprising 12 two-bedroom apartments.

Two-bedroom nurses' bungalows at ANSECO and Agorve were also identified, alongside a two-unit chamber-and-hall apartment attached to the classroom project at Sodzi.

Road infrastructure projects included the Hotorwovi Road at Atiehefe and the construction of a 10-kilometre road at Kome/Alakple.

The team also inspected an AstroTurf project at Hogbe Park as part of sports infrastructure development in the district.

According to the communication team, the 16 projects were at different stages of implementation, with some completed and others still under construction.

Mr Agbleze's team said the wider monitoring exercise across the four districts was aimed at establishing the location, status and progress of development interventions rather than relying solely on reports about their implementation.

The Regional Communication team said it would continue monitoring projects across the Volta Region to provide the public with information on their progress and expected benefits.

It maintained that first-hand verification would help communication officers provide more accurate accounts of development interventions while strengthening public awareness, transparency and accountability surrounding projects being implemented in communities across the region.

St. Monica’s SHS has secured qualification to the One-Eighth Stage of the 2026 National Science and Maths Quiz (NSMQ) after edging Amenfiman SHS in a closely fought contest at the SMS Auditorium.

St. Monica’s finished with 40 points, just three points ahead of Amenfiman SHS, who ended on 37 points. Tema Methodist Day SHS placed third with 15 points.

St. Monica’s announced their intentions from the very first round, taking an early lead with 12 points, ahead of Amenfiman SHS on 17 points and Tema Methodist Day SHS on 8 points.

St. Monica’s responded in Round Two, moving ahead with 21 points, while Amenfiman slipped to 16 points and Tema Methodist Day remained on 8 points.

The Problem of the Day further boosted St. Monica’s, who secured 6 points compared to Amenfiman’s 2, while Tema Methodist Day SHS failed to score.

St. Monica’s then extended their advantage in Round Three with an impressive 27 points, while Amenfiman managed 18 points and Tema Methodist Day SHS added 8 points.

The final True or False round saw St. Monica’s hold on to their lead and finish on 40 points. Amenfiman’s late effort took them to 37 points, while Tema Methodist Day SHS ended on 15 points.

St. Monica’s SHS has now booked their ticket to the One-Eighth Stage, with Amenfiman SHS narrowly missing out after leading the contest at the end of the opening round.

Ghana News.title: Why celebrate $2.62bn FDI while losing $1.7bn under the Domestic Gold Programme? IERPP asks
Ghana News.content:
Prof. Isaac Boadi Executive Director Institute of Economic Research and Public Policy (IERPP)

The Institute of Economic Research and Public Policy (IERPP) has welcomed Ghana’s reported US$2.62 billion in Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), saying it is an encouraging sign that international investors still find opportunities and potential in the Ghanaian economy in 2025.

But the Institute says the joy must be tempered with a sober assessment of the huge financial losses involved in the Domestic Gold Purchase Program (DGPP).

“Certainly, we should acknowledge Ghana’s capacity to draw US$2.62 billion in foreign direct investment,” said Prof. Isaac Boadi, Executive Director of IERPP. It is a sign that in spite of the economic challenges we are experiencing, international investors still have confidence in the opportunities in Ghana."

"But we cannot be happy about the money flowing into the economy when we are not looking at the big losses happening in the economy.”

Based on the figures that have emerged from the recent discussions on the DGPP, the program lost an estimated GH¢22 billion, which is about US$1.7 billion.

The comparison with the US$2.62 billion FDI figure is striking when set against the reported DGPP loss of a similar magnitude (around 65% of the value of Ghana’s FDI inflows).

“Every US$1 that Ghana attracts in FDI, the reported loss under the Domestic Gold Purchase Program is equivalent to about 65 cents,” Prof. Boadi observed."

“Not that the FDI was lost or that GoldBod was responsible for the entire loss of US$1.7 billion. The point is to show the magnitude of the loss relative to the capital we are celebrating.”

The IERPP emphasizes the importance of this distinction. The US$1.7 billion figure reported refers to losses under the DGPP as a program and cannot be directly attributed in its entirety to GoldBod. But the costs and fees associated with GoldBod identified as part of the programme’s losses must also be properly subject to public scrutiny.

The question is not whether we should celebrate FDI. “We certainly should,” Prof. Boadi said. “The question is, are we paying enough attention to how well we manage and protect the resources that we already have in our economy?”

The Institute argues that foreign investment remains vital to Ghana’s economic transformation. FDI can support job creation, technology transfer, productive capacity, infrastructure and foreign-exchange generation. But attracting foreign capital, IERPP cautions, cannot substitute for prudent management of public resources.

“Imagine filling a bucket with water while leaving a large hole at the bottom,” Prof. Boadi explained. “It would be good news that more water is being poured into the bucket, but the greater responsibility is to ask why we are allowing such a significant amount to escape.”

IERPP is therefore calling for greater transparency regarding the reported DGPP losses, including a clear breakdown of the sources of the losses, the costs incurred, the revenues generated, the role of GoldBod-related fees and charges, and the ultimate fiscal impact on the state.

The Institute also believes that Ghana’s accountability institutions, Parliament, civil society organisations, think tanks and the media have a responsibility to interrogate the figures with the same intensity with which positive economic developments are celebrated.

“There should be no selective enthusiasm when it comes to Ghana’s economic numbers,” Prof. Boadi said.

“When the figures are positive, we must celebrate them; when the figures reveal significant losses, we must ask difficult questions. Both are necessary for a credible economic conversation.”

IERPP maintains that genuine investor confidence is not built merely by attracting foreign capital. It is also built by demonstrating that Ghana has strong institutions, transparent public financial management and the capacity to safeguard economic resources.

“We must celebrate Ghana attracting US$2.62 billion in FDI,” Prof. Boadi said.

“But at the same time, we must have the courage to ask why a reported US$1.7 billion loss under the domestic gold programme is equivalent to almost two-thirds of that inflow. Ghana needs both investment and accountability. One without the other cannot deliver sustainable economic transformation.”

Ghana News.title: COKA urges NPP executives to return to party’s core values ahead of 2028
Ghana News.content:
Chairman Odeneho Kwaku Appiah

Newly elected Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Odeneho Kwaku Appiah, popularly known as COKA, has called on constituency vice-chairpersons in the region to recommit themselves to the party’s core values of discipline, integrity, responsibility and hard work.

Speaking at an engagement with constituency executives in Kumasi, Mr Appiah said the NPP’s historical appeal to Ghanaians and its electoral successes were built on these values, which he said must be restored to strengthen the party.

“I am urging all of us to go back to our roots, where we exemplified the ideals of discipline, integrity, responsibility and hard work,” he said.

He said the party must prioritise reconciliation, rebuild its structures and strengthen grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2028 general elections.

Mr Appiah noted that the NPP lost more than 1.1 million votes in the Ashanti Region in the 2024 elections, attributing the decline largely to low voter turnout rather than a complete loss of support for the party.

He therefore urged constituency vice-chairpersons to work closely with their chairpersons and other executives to reconnect with disillusioned supporters and revitalise the party’s grassroots structures.

He said the ongoing engagements were also intended to build unity within the party and position its 2028 presidential candidate, Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, for victory.

Responding on behalf of the executives, Mampong Constituency Vice-Chairperson, S. O. Frimpong, commended Mr Appiah for what he described as his proactive approach to post-election reconciliation.

He said Mr Appiah’s outreach to his main electoral opponents and other defeated aspirants demonstrated a commitment to an inclusive administration, adding that such efforts were critical to strengthening cohesion and restoring confidence among NPP supporters in the Ashanti Region.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
